Summary: TPS Lab Bug - Printing Multiple Gift Receipts
Description:
When you choose multiple individual items within a transaction to print gift receipts for, only one prints and not multiple. Is there a way to prompt for how many are needed? When going to the “Transactions” section to reprint as well, you can only print one before the system not allowing another one. Please see the steps below: 

*Need more than one on Individual items*

# Start a transaction and ring several items. 
# Choose the “options” for one of the items and choose gift receipt. 
# Choose another individual item, choose options and choose gift receipt.
# When you complete the transaction, only one prints even though two items were chosen and two were needed (i.e a grandmother purchases two items for two different grandchildren and needs to give two).

*Reprinting only One from the Transactions Section* 

# Go to Transactions. 
# Choose “gift receipt” next to the top transaction.
# One will print, then the option becomes “greyed out” and not able to happen again.

Summary: IOrderMgmtService.reserveItem() Not Invoked When Updating Quantity for SHIP_TO_STORE or BISPIS Items
Description:
In JMC, the {{ReserveItemEndpoint}} is responsible for reserving order items and is invoked in the following scenarios:

* Adding a *DELIVERY* item to the cart
* Adding a *SHIP_TO_STORE* item to the cart
* Adding a *BISPIS* item to the cart
* Updating the quantity of a *DELIVERY* line item in the cart

However, the {{ReserveItemEndpoint}} is *not* invoked in these scenarios:

* Updating the quantity of a *SHIP_TO_STORE* line item in the cart
* Updating the quantity of a *BISPIS* line item in the cart

Given that {{ReserveItemEndpoint}} is triggered when updating *DELIVERY* quantities, I believe the missing behavior for *SHIP_TO_STORE* and *BISPIS* may be a bug in JMC. Both types still need to reserve inventory to ensure availability is accurately reflected.

If this is considered a feature enhancement rather than a defect, I apologize for the mislabeling. I’m happy to open a new ticket as an ‘Idea’ if needed—just let me know.



NOTE: The attached logs are from my intelliJ.  IOrderMgmtService.reserveItem() is invoked when the SHIP_TO_STORE order line item gets added, but not when the quantity is changed.

Summary: Shift Change - till balance issue
Description:
A standard store would have a user open the store/till and running transactions in the morning, perform a shift change and hand off to a new user will take responsibility for the rest of the day and close till/store. Business request that each user is accountable for their till during their shift and shouldn’t have a variance (if occurred) to carry over to the next user
e.g.

Store 9712 and reg 1: 

# User 9999 logs in and open store and till - Starting Float: $100 (Tran# 2890-2893, *attached image-1*)
# User 9999 did one transaction $50 cash (Tran# 2894, *attached image-2*)
# SHIFT CHANGE (Tran# 2895-2897)
# Entered $145 with -$5.00 variance tied to user 9999 (*attached image-3*)
# At this point, user 9999 logs off and passes it onto user 27583. (*attached image-4*)
# If we check till expected cash total is still at $150 instead of previous user 9999 counted total$145
This cause the next user to be short the $5 and once they reconcile and close the till, it will count towards till accountability, even if they collected the correct amount of change during their shift.
# Continuing with the user 27583 and did another $50 sale (Tran# 2898)
# counted the drawer after closing till to $195 (-$5.00 for the day) a variance will show up again since the till isn’t reset after shift change to $145. (Tran# 2899-2903, *attached* *image-5 and image-6*)

Variance should be separate out after the shift-change and update the till balance to match what was counted during the shift change. The variance will need to carry over into the closing amount for the deposit.

Breakdown of accountability within request from example above.

User 9999 Variance: -$5.00

User 27583 Variance: $0.00

Deposit Variance: -$5.00

Summary: Provide an 'All Brands' option in Promote similar to the 'All Items' option
Description:
From the below issue encountered, 
”_Jumpmind Promote is treating any “Coupon” spark as an individual item. This seems to be happening with vanity/coupon codes, not single-use codes.  This came up as an issue during this past weekend’s BOGO 50% Off All Items promotion. I saw this issue on retail, but did not get to test it on web._

_The promo setup had Item Inclusions set to All Items (screenshot 1), since all items we sell were part of the BOGO. If a single item is added to bag on retail, and then a coupon code is entered (in this case, 20% off $50 code JUNGRS25), Jumpmind thinks this code is an item, and it triggers the BOGO 50% Off All items promotion (Screenshot 2). As a result, single items were getting a 50% discount. I was able to fix this by adding the coupon code as an exclusion to the promotion, but ideally the system wouldn’t treat a coupon code an as item.”_


In this case, we were able to fix the issue by adding that vanity code as an exclusion to the promotion, but this wouldn't be a long-term solution for us. At any given time, we could have several vanity codes live, and it would be easy to miss some.

For this particular BOGO All promo, a reusable item group wouldn’t work; it would be difficult to account for all possible item inclusions and exclusions.

Is there any way to create an ‘All Brands’ option instead of 'All Items'?

Summary: Enable Auto-Close for POS terminals
Description:
JDNA has requested a new feature that will automatically close all devices within an store and also automate store closing and baking processes. Assuming the associates don’t close the device, this process would initiate after midnight and move the devices/store to the next business date, but also automatically publish the store closing and banking transactions. 

When associates don’t close stores / devices properly they can ring transactions on incorrect business dates which causes issues in 3rd party financial systems. Also, if the store closing/deposit transactions aren’t published then that also causes issues in 3rd party financial systems. 

Opening this as “highest” priority as client has expressed a desire to get this functionality within the next few months.

Summary: Jumpmind PROD PostgreSQL Central Repository - Potential Performance Issue
Description:
Synopsis:  The “database signature” from Jumpmind PROD is drastically “worse” with significantly more blocking, update, commits, etc after increasing the publisher pods from 1 to 10.   Database system CPU also seemed to “triple”.  It seems there is an UPDATE query that is executing at a rate of approximately 8000 times per SECOND!!  My theory is that these pods are “looking for work” at a rate of 800 times per second per pod.  If that is true, we should be able to reduce that rate to about 10 times per second per pod.  During our holiday peak, we have seen transactions per second in the 60’s so 10 pods “looking for work” 10 times per second should be able to easily handle that load.

 

The load we have today coming from the stores when we were researching this was around 2 transactions per second.  We should not be seeing this kind of database load ☹

Summary: Few pay in transactions are not added to till reconciliation report
Description:
There was a prod store 195 reg 3 reporting that pay in data did not get generated in the till reconciliation report on 7/14. Store made a pay_in transaction of 50$ on reg 3 but it wasn't shown in the report. Attached a screenshot of the data in the DB and the report for reference.

*Query used to get the pay in data* - 

{noformat}(
    select COALESCE(SUM(LI.TENDER_AMOUNT), 0)
    from TransModel as T
    join TenderLineItemModel as LI
        on LI.DEVICE_ID = T.DEVICE_ID
        and LI.BUSINESS_DATE = T.BUSINESS_DATE
        and LI.SEQUENCE_NUMBER = T.SEQUENCE_NUMBER
    where T.BUSINESS_DATE = ${businessDate}
        and T.BUSINESS_UNIT_ID = ${businessUnitId}
        and T.TILL_ID = ${tillId}
        and T.TRANS_STATUS = 'COMPLETED'
        and T.TRANS_TYPE = 'PAY_IN'
        and LI.VOIDED = 0
        and T.SESSION_ID =
            (select SESSION_ID from TransModel where CREATE_TIME = (
                select MAX(CREATE_TIME) from TransModel where TRANS_TYPE = 'OPEN_TILL' and TRANS_STATUS = 'COMPLETED' and BUSINESS_DATE = ${businessDate} and BUSINESS_UNIT_ID = ${businessUnitId} and TILL_ID = ${tillId})
                    and TRANS_TYPE = 'OPEN_TILL' and TRANS_STATUS = 'COMPLETED' and BUSINESS_DATE = ${businessDate} and BUSINESS_UNIT_ID = ${businessUnitId} and TILL_ID = ${tillId})
) {noformat}

In the above query, since the session id for the pay in transaction was null, the record wasn't picked and shown in the report. We noticed the session id is populated for most of the pay in transactions but for some it is set as null. 


*We have two queries from our end:*

# Is there any reason for filtering the pay in data based on session id?
# Why session id isn't populated for some pay in records?

Summary: Create separate config to control the "Reconcile this till?" prompt
Description:
*Background*: Right now, the same config ({{openpos.ops.till.promptForTillClose}}) is used to control both the “Close this till?” and “Reconcile this till?” Prompt. 

*Requirement*: BBW wants to disable only the “Reconcile this till?” prompt. 

*Current solution*: We have set {{promptForTillClose}} to false and overrode {{CloseTillStateHelper}} to directly enable the “Close this till?” prompt by removing the {{isTillClosePrompted()}} check from {{doNextAction}}()

*Feature request*: We would like base JMC to create a separate configs for disabling the “Reconcile this till?” and “Close this till?” prompts, so that they are not dependent on each other.
Comments:

Summary: TPS Transaction Bug - Return Tender Issue
Description:
We had a larger return issue happen with a transaction over the weekend. 

* *Store #0043 Reg 004 Transaction #1875* was a return that was completed on 3/14/24. This was an employee return and they reached out to us b/c they have not seen the funds return to their card. They are claiming they presented their credit card via Apple Pay to get the funds back on their credit card.
* When we look in the database on the sls_transaction_summery table, we are seeing the funds were actually returned to the “GIFT_CERTIFICATE” payment type, which is  that “alternate tender” and/or Hallmark Rewards Dollar payment type.

*_TLDR;_* 

* In a return transaction, where a voided line item is a MANUFACTURER_COUPON, the return tender gets returned back to this voided payment method, RATHER than the original form of payment. From a store’s perspective, they are seeing “Card” as an option and running through the motions as normal as well – so they aren’t able to see this until after the return has been completed and funds are never received.



*_Longer Explanation;_* *Store #0043 Reg 004 Transaction #1875 was a return that was completed on 3/14/24*

8 receipted  return items 

3 sale items 

2 other voided sale items 

1 "Employee" item

Sum total of all this (tax included) is indeed -31.44.

 

*This voided item looks like it was added because the sale items were Hallmark Cards:*

1 *voided* MANUFACTURER_COUPON 

"familyCode": "HMK" 

"itemDescription": "Buy 2 Hallmark cards Get 1 FREE equal or lesser value up to $3.99 Easter 24"

 "saveValue": 251.00,
  "saveValueType": "CENTS_OFF_TRANSACTION_TOTAL",

*"posItemId": "786524988"*

*Not sure why it was voided, but  this item is almost certainly the root of the problem.*

TENDER:

The 31.44 was refunded on ONE tender: Tender_Code=HMK_REWARD using certificate number *786524988,* which directly matches the ItemId of the voided Coupon item. I did some further digging into the SA archive and the tender on the original sale transaction was MasterCard, and not HMK_REWARD. (0043-003 seq 261 on Feb 23, so it was a sale rung up on a JM device).

 *_There is nothing in the JSON that shows any other tender was attempted on the return._*



We need to make sure we are NEVER returning to a MANUFACTURER_COUPON - how can we make this happen and avoid an issue like above happening again?

Summary: Tender Anytime - POS system to automatically apply pre-tendered data during the payment process and completely skip the Tender options screen
Description:
*Requirement Request/Description:*  
Implement functionality where, if a tender is pre-tendered as part of the "tender anytime" feature, the POS system automatically skips the tender options screen and uses the pre-tendered tender data for completing the transaction. The option to choose a different tender type or form of payment should not be available once pre-tendering is completed, except in cases where the payment is declined or the pre-tendered card does not have sufficient funds. In such cases, the system should return to the tender screen to allow the selection of an alternative payment method.

*Story Summary:*  
As a cashier, I want the POS system to automatically apply pre-tendered tender data during the payment process so that the tender options screen is bypassed and the transaction is completed using the pre-tendered data. (Note the tender options screen might be visible for a couple seconds but no button selection is required)  However, if the payment is declined or the tendered card has insufficient funds, the system should return to the tender screen for an alternate payment selection.

*Data Requirements:*  

# The POS must bypass the tender options screen if pre-tendered data exists.
# The system should return to the tender screen only if the pre-tendered payment is declined or insufficient funds are detected.

*Tech Notes:*  

*Acceptance Criteria:*  

# If a tender is pre-tendered and the cashier selects Tender, the POS must skip the tender options screen and use the pre-tendered data to process the payment. 
# If the pre-tendered payment is declined, the POS should return to the tender screen, allowing the cashier to select an alternative payment method. 
# If the swiped GC has insufficient funds, the POS should debit the remaining balance and prompt for a different type of tender to cover the rest of the transaction.

*Mock-Ups/Renderings/Screenshots:*  

# The "Tap/Insert/Swipe" prompt on the POS system:
# Payment device after a credit / debit card that requires a pin is used to tender:

Summary: Do not show price override discount amount in VirtualReceiptHelper if this config (itemPriceOverride.isDisplayedAsDiscount) is set to false.
Description:
When we set this config ({{openpos.sell.sellItemActionHandlers.itemPriceOverride.isDisplayedAsDiscount}}) to false, the total discount does not add up the amount from price overrides in the Sell screen. This is done in {{TenderTotalsCalculator}} → {{getDiscountTotal}}(). 

However, In {{VirtualReceiptHelper}} → {{populateRequest}}(), the {{request.totalDiscountsOrCredits}}() uses transaction.getDiscountTotal(). This includes the discount amount from price overrides. We need to exclude price override discount amount here as well.

In BBW, we’ve overridden VirtualReceiptHelper and used tenderTotalsCalculator.getDiscountTotal() in order to fix this.

Summary: SymDS application restarts with OOM issue
Description:
We have few instances where SymDS application gets restarts with Out-of-Memory (OOM) issue in production. I did analyze the couldn’t find anything odd but I looked in the code block (see attached) of SymDS application and below is my observation (I could be wrong so please execuse me). 
1. *Long-lived References to* {{ProcessInfo}}

If {{this.statisticManager.newProcessInfo(...)}} registers or stores the {{ProcessInfo}} in a cache, registry, or monitoring structure *without purging it*, it could result in a *memory leak over time*. (my wild guess but could be wrong)

2. *Large* {{batchList}}

If {{loadDataFromTransport(...)}} loads *a large amount of data* into memory (e.g., {{batchList}} with thousands of batches), and:

* The objects have large payloads,
* The method runs frequently, and GC pressure is high,

# *Unclosed Input/Output Streams*


Also We wanted to enable the console log in SymDS application. Can please let  us know the configuration which enable the console log  in SymDS application.

12/Aug/25 11:05 AM;70121:4c55edb8-b2f0-47f8-bb2c-524b3fa93eda;The wrapper.log typically shows up in the logs folder of the SymmetricDS installation directory. If you cannot find them there, I would recommend checking the sym_service.conf file in the conf directory of your SymmetricDS installation location, as it contains the following section you can reference to find your logs:



{noformat}#********************************************************************
# Wrapper Logging Properties
#********************************************************************

# Log file to use for wrapper output logging.
wrapper.logfile=logs/wrapper.log

# Wrapper process ID
wrapper.pidfile=tmp/wrapper.pid

# SymmetricDS process ID
wrapper.server.pidfile=tmp/server.pid

# Log level (SEVERE, WARNING, INFO, CONFIG, FINE, FINER, FINEST)
wrapper.logfile.loglevel=INFO

SELECT
    s.calls,
    s.mean_time,
    e.query_id,
    q.query_sql_text
FROM
    query_store.runtime_stats AS s
JOIN
    query_store.runtime_stats_entries AS e
    ON s.runtime_stats_entry_id = e.runtime_stats_entry_id
JOIN
    query_store.query_texts AS q
    ON e.query_id = q.query_text_id
WHERE
    s.start_time >= NOW() - INTERVAL '2 hours'
ORDER BY
    s.mean_time DESC
LIMIT 20;

and 



WITH recent_stats AS (
    SELECT
        s.calls,
        s.mean_time,
        e.query_id,
        q.query_sql_text,
        (s.mean_time * s.calls) AS total_exec_time
    FROM
        query_store.runtime_stats AS s
    JOIN
        query_store.runtime_stats_entries AS e
        ON s.runtime_stats_entry_id = e.runtime_stats_entry_id
    JOIN
        query_store.query_texts AS q
        ON e.query_id = q.query_text_id
    WHERE
        s.start_time >= NOW() - INTERVAL '2 hours'
)
SELECT
    query_id,
    query_sql_text,
    calls,
    ROUND(mean_time, 2) AS mean_time_ms,
    ROUND(total_exec_time, 2) AS total_exec_time_ms,
    ROUND(100 * total_exec_time / SUM(total_exec_time) OVER (), 2) AS pct_of_load
FROM
    recent_stats
ORDER BY
    total_exec_time DESC
LIMIT 20;

  coalesce(sum(i.FOREIGN_CURRENCY_AMOUNT), 0) as total_original_tender_amount,
  coalesce(sum(i.CASH_BACK_AMOUNT), 0) as total_tender_cash_back
  from sls_tender ten
  inner join sls_tender_line_item i
  on ten.TENDER_CODE = i.TENDER_CODE
  inner join sls_trans t
  on i.SEQUENCE_NUMBER = t.SEQUENCE_NUMBER
  and i.DEVICE_ID = t.DEVICE_ID
  and i.BUSINESS_DATE = t.BUSINESS_DATE
  where
  t.SESSION_ID = $3 and
  t.TRANS_STATUS = 'COMPLETED' and
  i.VOIDED = 0
  group by ten.DESCRIPTION, t.SESSION_ID, ten.TENDER_CODE, ten.TENDER_TYPE_CODE, i.ISO_CURRENCY_CODE, i.ISO_FOREIGN_CURRENCY_CODE)

Description:

On 6/11, QA tested Open/Close Day 1 scenario, Till Reports show Register 1 has 0 cent rounding, Register 2 has -0.03.  Daily Sale report for the entire store has rounding amount -0.05.

Description: The vertex pod in production is only used to run a RTE to JMC Vertex job that loads the tax data for the stores, it is not used otherwise, the logs we see in Datadog also doesn't have any activities post the job, but we are seeing a constant ~4GB of memory usage for the vertex pod, attached are the logs and couple of screenshots, would want to know what is using this memory up in vertex.

Here are some suggestions to narrow down what’s using the memory:

# *Check JVM Heap Settings*

* Look at the Vertex pod startup flags ({{-Xms}}, {{-Xmx}}). If {{-Xmx4g}}, that explains the ~4GB footprint.
* You can confirm by checking GC logs or by looking at a heap dump ({{jmap -heap}} or similar).

# *Heap Dump Analysis*

* Trigger a heap dump after the job completes.
* Analyze with tools like Eclipse MAT or jvisualvm to see if large objects remain.

# *Compare Pre-Job vs. Post-Job Heap*

* Run the pod, check memory before the job, then after the job.
* If the increase is permanent, the job is retaining data.

# *Datadog JVM Integration*

* Enable Datadog’s JVM integration to view heap breakdown (young gen, old gen, metaspace, etc.).

Most likely the Vertex pod JVM is configured with {{-Xmx4g}}, so it reserves ~4GB heap at startup. Even though the job is idle, that memory stays allocated. It’s not necessarily a leak, just how Java memory management works in containerized environments.

Summary: Discrepancy in Tax Calculation Between Item-Level and Order-Level Calculations
Description:
We have identified a discrepancy when calculating tax at the per-item level versus on the total taxable amount.  

*Example Scenario:*  

* 5 items, each priced at: *30*  
* Per-item tax calculated (at applicable rate): *1.43 each* → *Total: 7.15*  
* Tax calculated on overall price (150): *7.14*  
* Difference: *0.01*  

*Issue:*  
Currently, the system (JumpMind) appears to be summing up the rounded per-item taxes, resulting in 7.15. However, when calculating tax at the order level (on total taxable amount) and then rounding, the correct result should be 7.14. This leads to an overcharge of 0.01 in this example.  

Although the variance seems small per transaction, it accumulates significantly across multiple transactions and stores, which could lead to compliance and audit  issues.

*Impact:*  

* Compliance risk with tax regulations.  (Raised by Audit / finance team)

*Expected Behavior:*  
The tax calculation should be aligned with the correct rounding methodology — either calculate tax at the total order level or adjust per-item rounding to avoid discrepancies between the two methods.  

----

Summary: Swagger UI Fails to Load due to SpringDoc–Spring Framework Incompatibility
Description:
After deploying the new Jumpmind build (Jumpmind Commerce 243.1.30 ), Swagger UI fails to load API definitions. The error message displayed is:

{noformat}Failed to load API definition.
Errors
Fetch error
response status is 500 /v3/api-docs/API{noformat}

*Key Findings:*

* *SpringDoc OpenAPI version:* 2.4.0
* *Spring Framework version:* 6.2.6
* *Root Cause:* SpringDoc OpenAPI 2.4.0 is *incompatible* with Spring Framework 6.2.6.
** SpringDoc 2.4.0 was designed for Spring Framework 6.1.x.
** The error originates from {{NoSuchMethodError}} in {{ControllerAdviceBean.<init>}}, caused by a constructor signature change between Spring Framework 6.1.x and 6.2.6.

Summary: SymDS rule creation inquiry for dev_device table
Description:
We are encountering issues with 60x registers where the system time is incorrect, resulting in suspended transactions having an end time earlier than the start time. These transactions are failing to process in SAP.

Upon investigation, we found that the dev_device table on these registers retains outdated timezone data even after the system time is corrected. Deleting the dev_device record and rebooting the register resolves the issue, as the timezone is updated and correctly synced to central.

Since approximately 600+ registers are affected, we tested a solution in a non-production environment by creating a sync rule in SymDS that allows data in the dev_device table to sync from central to the registers. This approach enables us to centrally update the timezone data while the infrastructure team updates the system time on the devices. The test also included validation of sym_outgoing and sym_incoming batches and everything worked as expected.

Could you please confirm if it’s okay to proceed with creating this rule in production? Are there any potential risks or considerations we should be aware of before implementing it?

Attached few screenshots for your reference.

Summary: Return Transactions Fail When Central Office (CO) is Down
Description:
We have observed an issue in Jumpmind POS during return transactions:

* *Scenario:* When performing a return, the POS validates the sale invoice against the Central Office (CO) system and Oracle CO DB (via bridge).
* *Issue:* If the CO is down or unavailable, the POS displays an error:
_"Invoice not found."_
* *Impact:* In this situation, return transactions cannot be processed, including those where the original sale was made at the same store. Since a large percentage of returns are performed at the same store, this leads to significant operational challenges when CO is not accessible.

h3. *Request for Assistance:*

# Is there an existing mechanism or recommended approach in Jumpmind POS to allow return processing when the CO is down?
# How can this be handled to ensure minimal disruption to store operations?
# What are the implications or considerations for implementing such a mechanism (if available)?

h3. *Business Impact:*

* Return transactions are blocked during CO downtime.
* Causes delays in customer service and operational inefficiencies.
* High dependency on CO availability for routine store operations.

# Or successfully moved file will also remain in the local directory if flow fails? This will get repicked in next run and create duplicate on remote SFTP server?

11/Sep/25 6:23 AM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;1 - No, the Text File Writer (component doing the write to sftp) only takes data as input and outputs it to another location in a text file.  It is not doing a 'file' action.  Metl works on messages of data so as it reads the data out of the local file it sends that data over to the other location to generate the new file.  If you look at the flow the step before the write is just a text file reader meaning it is just opening the source file reading the contents line by line and pushing that data to the writer which then creates a new file with that content.  

2 - The transfer of data happens in batches but refer to #1, it is not a batch of multiple files, rather batches of the content of files.

3 - Yes, successfully moved data (which could be complete file contents) would remain if the flow fails on any subsequent file read records.  Yes, if the target file is removed prior to the flow running again and attempting to push the file later it will push the same file again.

"Action on Success" and "Action on Error" are both flow completion level activities, meaning once the flow determines all steps / components have completed OR if at any point an Error happens that causes the flow to stop, then it will perform one of those actions.

At quick thought I believe you probably have at least 2 options.

# You could do the write to sftp in a groovy script where you handle the whole process where you could monitor if you've pushed an entire file over and if so remove the source at that point before pushing the next file. Or build a list of successful files as it runs and then make use of the OnSuccess or OnError part of the groovy script to do the clean up action there.
# You could possibly make use of the Error Suspense Step on the writer which would capture errored records and send them down to a different component where you'd have to filter and determine what to do with them.  The challenge I see with this option is if the error happens in the middle of pushing a file, the captured 'error' records may only be part of a file.  Be aware that using the Error Suspense Step property will prevent that particular step from ever causing the whole flow to error.

Summary: Store cannot be opened due to time zone mismatch in ops_unit_status entries
Description:
TVS’s central JMC instance is configured with a time zone that is 2 hours ahead of the store.

Last week, TVS closed the store while the iPads were failed over to the cloud. This action created an entry in {{ops_unit_status}} with a {{create_time}} generated in the central cloud JMC instance. Symmetric DS then synced this row down to the store.

When the tester attempted to open the store on the fixed register (which was not failed over to the cloud), nothing happened in the UI. The *Open Store* button did not change to *Close Store*, and the application did not enable the *Open Device* button. As a result, the tester was unable to open the store.

*Investigation Details*

The store status is determined by invoking {{GetStoreStatusEndpoint}}. Within this method, the {{opsRepository}} is used to fetch the data:

{{List<UnitStatusModel> status = this.opsRepository.findUnitStatus(UnitType.STORE.name(), (String)null, businessUnitId);}}

The implementation of {{findUnitStatus(UnitType.STORE.name(), (String)null, businessUnitId)}} returns only the most recent status.

Since the iPad was failed over to the cloud, and because the cloud instance is set to a time zone 2 hours ahead, the fixed instance was reporting the store as *CLOSED*. This occurred because the most recent entry in {{ops_unit_status}} had a {{UNIT_STATUS}} of *CLOSED*, despite attempts to open the store.

The tester would have to wait 2 hours after the store was closed to successfully open the store.

Summary: The issue is with Auto Updater. While running, it deletes the Symmetric staging in/out files, which causes synchronization failures. As a result, incoming batches fail and sales are posted under the wrong business date.
Description: The problem area has been identified as *Auto Updater*. When Auto Updater is running, it deletes the Symmetric staging area in/out files. Because the batches fail, the system continues to operate on the old business date, leading to sales being posted under the incorrect business date. This issue directly impacts transactional accuracy and creates a mismatch between actual and reported sales. Attached are the logs files.

06/Jan/26 4:23 AM;712020:877ebe8a-e44a-419d-b0bd-b385e6a816f3;*Key Log Findings :* 


Multiple errors indicate *order pricing, promo, and pre-auth tables are missing*:

{noformat}ERROR [TriggerRouterService] Table not found: sls_order_pre_auth
ERROR [TriggerRouterService] Table not found: sls_order_price_mod
ERROR [TriggerRouterService] Table not found: sls_order_promo_code_line_item
ERROR [TriggerRouterService] Table not found: sls_order_status_trans{noformat}

When these tables are unavailable, POS *cannot correctly rehydrate original sale pricing and promo allocation during return*, especially for *card-based tenders*



These errors confirm *state reconstruction problems* during the return flow:

{noformat}Data could not be converted to CustomerModel object. Action.getDate() returned: null{noformat}

The refund discrepancy during partial return to original tender occurs because the POS is unable to retrieve original sale pricing and promo allocation due to missing order pricing, promo, and pre-authorization tables ({{sls_order_price_mod}}, {{sls_order_promo_code_line_item}}, {{sls_order_pre_auth}}).

As a result, the system recalculates the refund using rounded per-unit values instead of the exact original captured amount, causing small rounding deltas. This only affects *card refunds*, as cash and merch credit do not rely on original tender reconciliation.

Description:
We are observing an issue in Jumpmind POS publisher framework while processing messages from the queue. The framework inserts data into the {{pubeng_queue}} table and acquires a row lock during processing. However, we are seeing messages like:



Unlocking due to current time (2025-09-18T07:49:09.535066011) past lockExpirationTime (2025-09-18T07:39:25.021095)



Because of this, most of the messages are failing to process successfully and, after 5 retry attempts, are being moved into the {{pubeng_dead_letter_queue}}.

We have observed that *as the number of stores has increased, and with it the transaction volume to be published, this issue has become more frequent*.

*Impact:*

* Critical subscriber systems are impacted, specifically *RTLOG (Finance system)* and *Oracle POS*, which are not receiving the published data on time.
* This is causing data delivery delays and risk of missing or inconsistent information between Jumpmind POS and downstream systems.

*Request:*
We need clarification and resolution on:

# Why the lock expiration is happening before message processing completes.
# Whether this is due to configuration (e.g., lock expiration settings), performance bottleneck, or a code-level issue.
# How to prevent messages from moving into the dead letter queue and ensure timely delivery to RTLOG and Oracle POS subscribers.

22/Sep/25 7:40 AM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;As long as you don’t plan on making updates or changes to the flows or models, you could just create a new folder and agent on the Deploy tab.  Inside this new agent you need to update every resource to point to your new folders and databases making sure to have them different than your prod.  That is open every single resource and update every field at least once to make sure it is using its' own copy of the resource.

This way, you are running the identical flows that would have run for production just with different resources.

Otherwise, if you want a full other Metl instance you could just copy the Metl config database to another db/schema and then you have a duplicate copy of production (after pointing the new Metl to this new db).  Note you cannot make changes directly in that environment or they will become out of sync with the real production.  You’d have to migrate flow updates like you would from dev to test to prod.  It would go dev to test to prod and prod copy.  If changes are ever made in prod they would also have to be exported and imported back into prod copy otherwise you will be running different versions and will run the risk of the flows being out of sync not being able to import in the future.

Summary: Reason for messages moving to DLQ
Description:
Hi,

Currently there are 382K messages in DLQ of Azure Service Bus “jmctranspayload” used by “JMC Transaction Publisher” and “RTLog” flows. Could you please help us understand on,

# What conditions does these messages go to DLQ?
# Is there a retry conditions for it?
# How to set up auto delete in case there is expired data in it?

Thanks & Regards,

Rahul Jain
Comments:
23/Sep/25 8:27 AM;qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:8ce0c324-1b4a-4d0e-a9a4-72a2288f72be;[^jmc-to-rtlog-with-oracle-lookup-JMC to RTLog with Oracle Lookup-flow.json]

[^web-services-JMC Transaction Publisher-flow.json]

04/Nov/25 3:18 PM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;[~accountid:qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:8ce0c324-1b4a-4d0e-a9a4-72a2288f72be] 
Messages end up in the DLQ for a specific queue if they cannot be delivered/processed successfully.
Common conditions are:

# Max Delivery Count Exceeded
Each message has a delivery count property. Every time the consumer receives a message and then abandons it (or processing fails without completing), the count increments.
If it reaches the MaxDeliveryCount (default = 10), the message is automatically moved to the DLQ.
# TTL (Time-To-Live) Expired
If a message's TTL expires (based on TimeToLive set either at the queue/subscription or per message), and EnableDeadLetteringOnMessageExpiration is true, it goes into DLQ.
# Potential Other Reasons
exceeding max header size, deserialization problems, or malformed messages.



Azure Service Bus automatically retries delivery of a message up to MaxDeliveryCount.  Each attempt increments the DeliveryCount property.
If the consumer keeps failing/abandoning, when it reaches the limit, the broker moves it to DLQ.



DLQ is just another queue — messages stay there until explicitly handled. 
Options:

Auto-delete on Expiration:

* Configure TimeToLive (TTL) on the main queue/subscription so messages that expire are not sent to DLQ unless EnableDeadLetteringOnMessageExpiration is set.

If you don’t need expired messages at all, disable dead-lettering on expiration.

DLQ Cleanup Jobs:

Use Azure Functions, Logic Apps, or a scheduled background job to periodically purge DLQ.

With SDKs (ServiceBusReceiver), you can connect to the DLQ (path: myqueue/$DeadLetterQueue) and CompleteAsync() (delete) messages.

Example using CLI:

{noformat}az servicebus queue delete --namespace-name <ns> --resource-group <rg> --name <queue-name>/$DeadLetterQueue{noformat}

Auto delete from the DLQ itself is not natively supported, you would need to write your own code to do the cleanup for this case.

Summary: DTLR: Add additional tenders to Order Create Flow
Description:
Currently, DTLR accepts Card (Credit Card) when creating an order. They would like to add two additional tenders: Gift Card and Cash.

* Card should remain as Pre_Auth
* Gift Card should be Purchase_Auth (funds captured when the order is created)
* Cash 

We attempted the following, but were unable to get it working:

* Added new buttons
* Added new sls_tender_policy
* Set ORDER_PURCHASE_AUTH.lineItemTypeCodes to Order_In_Store
* Updated openpos.orders.itemTenderGroup from ORDER_PRE_AUTH to ORDER_PURCHASE_AUTH

(We also cleared cache and bounced services.)

After these steps, only [CARD] is still listed as a tender when creating an order. Please see the attached .txt file with the scripts we used.



Would you be able to advise on how to properly add these additional tenders into the Order flow?

Description:

This discrepancy is caused by a technical problem with data replication between registers, resulting in some transactions not being synced correctly.

We have moved tmp folder out from C:\Jumpmind\point-of-sale.



During preliminary investigation, we observed some patterns that might be related to the issue; however, we are not certain if these findings fully explain the problem. Further analysis and expertise from your side would be helpful to confirm or rule out these points.



Jetty's HTTP request parser enforces a default limit on the number of form fields it will accept in a single request. The default maximum number of form fields allowed is *1000*. The following day, the store was opened from a different register. 24/Oct/25 10:07 AM;712020:d4626b4e-9ff3-475f-9c6e-8509649cd509;*internal*

This is a core JMC bug. The base JMC {{GetNextOrderEndpoint}} utilizes the {{GetNextRandomizedSequenceEndpoint}} to generate the Order Number. We create the randomized sequence number using a salted hash of a long created by appending the business unit id to the next sequence number from the DB. The issue is that we only generate the salt for the hash once, so that when the sequence numbers roll over, the exact same “random” sequence is generated. I was able to recreate this by altering my local DB to roll over and reuse the first sequence number.

Summary: Store closure status not updating in ops_unit_status table causing inconsistent store close indication
Description:
*Issue Summary:*

On 2025-09-30, the cashier successfully closed the store (store code: 60454, register: 551) at night. However, the next morning, the system still indicated that the store was not closed. The store team attempted to close the store again, and although the front-end showed a toast message confirming the store closure was successful, the system continued to display that the store was not closed.

*Investigation Findings:*

* Logs revealed an error where the system failed to insert the store close entry into the {{ops_unit_status}} table.
* The log showed a fallback from insert to update operation for the {{UnitStatusModel}} with status {{CLOSED}} and business date {{20250930}}.
* Manually inserting the missing entry into the {{ops_unit_status}} table resolved the issue temporarily.
* The issue appears related to a failure in persisting the store close status in the database, causing the front-end and back-end store status to go out of sync despite successful UI feedback.

*Impact:*

* Store status remains incorrectly open in the system after closure.
* Potential risk of data inconsistency and operational confusion.
* Manual intervention required to fix database state.

*Request:*

Please investigate the root cause of the failure to insert the store close status into the {{ops_unit_status}} table and provide a fix or workaround to prevent this issue from recurring.



*fixed logs:*

2025-09-30 23:38:26.338 INFO  [60454-551] [StateManagerThread8(pos:60454-551)] [TransSequenceHelper] Next 'TRANSACTION' sequence # acquired from ClientContext: 1182
2025-09-30 23:38:26.342 INFO  [60454-551] [StateManagerThread8(pos:60454-551)] [EndpointInvoker] IPublishService.publish()  
2025-09-30 23:38:26.349 INFO  [60454-551] [StateManagerThread8(pos:60454-551)] [DBSession] Insert of entity failed, failing over to an update: UnitStatusModel(deviceId=60454-551, businessUnitId=60454, sequenceNumber=1182, unitId=60454, unitType=STORE, unitStatus=CLOSED, businessDate=20250930)
2025-09-30 23:38:26.351 INFO  [60454-551] [StateManagerThread8(pos:60454-551)] [EndpointInvoker] IContextService.commitSequence()
Comments:
01/Oct/25 8:39 AM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;The issue was due to the key on the ops_unit_status table did not include business_date so in this case the exact combination of device_id, business_unit_id and sequence_number matched with an old record so the old record was updated however the open/close process makes use of the create time field to determine whether the store is open and in this case the updated row does not update the create time so it appeared to POS that the store was still open.

A more recent version of JMC updated the key structure on this table to include business_date.

I will follow up with engineering to confirm whether you can just add the PK to resolve this issue until you take a new version.
01/Oct/25 10:02 AM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;I have determined you cannot directly update the PK on that table, I have forwarded the issue to engineering to get the update ported back to 243.1.
02/Oct/25 1:44 PM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;The updates have been completed to fix this and will be part of the 243.1.31 release

Summary: TPS Lab Bug - Items not Returnable
Description:
We are having issues in our productions stores where they are unable to process items to be returned. These items are not flagged “non-returnable”, and in our return tables, we have them set to 60 days and also can be overridden if needed, yet when the store tries to process on receipt brought back 30+ days, the items are grey and say “ITEM CANNOT BE RETURNED”.

{noformat}select trans_hist_ref_in_days, * from sls_rtn_policy where return_policy_id like 'return%';{noformat}

08/Oct/25 2:23 PM;70121:4c55edb8-b2f0-47f8-bb2c-524b3fa93eda;This is how the excluded card types operates:

By putting a card type in the Excluded Card Types it prevents it from automatically processing a return on that type of card. When there is nothing in that list, and a return is done, it will pop up with a prompt and tell you how much is due to be returned on each card if there are multiple in the transaction. You can select one and then it will automatically return the value shown to that card. When there are multiple cards for one transaction, you will need to select each one individually.

When there is a card added to the Excluded card types list, this changes. Now, it will not prompt you to select a card. If there was only one card used for the transaction, and that card type is on the Excluded card types list, it will only show the amount due back, and upon clicking next, the payment device will say insert/tap card. Whatever card is tapped or inserted is the card that will have the amount returned to it, even if it is the same card used in the original transaction. This process is agnostic, and doesn’t care what card it is returning to.

In the event that there are multiple cards that were used in one transaction, and one of them is in the excluded list, it will show you all of the cards, but if the excluded one is selected, the pin pad will prompt for insert/tap the same as before. If the other card is then selected afterwards, it will still process automatically for that card. If you select the non-exluded card first, it will automatically process the same as before, but then when you select the card return option a second time, the amount will show, and when you click next, it will just prompt the pin pad for insert/tap, as the remaining card on the transaction is in the Excluded card types list.

25/Nov/25 1:20 PM;712020:6aedbc79-012d-44c8-9b26-7f19555e139d;This is my newbie analysis so far.  John V asked me to help determine what configuration values BBW should use to make debit cards require card presentation while keeping credit cards auto-returning to original card, focusing on Commerce-side config (not Aurus payment processing).

----

I looked at the commerce configuration logic to determine what values BBW should use for their requirement where debit cards require presentation and credit cards auto-return.

The core logic is *requiresMatchingCard = paymentService.result && !inExcludedList*, where:

* *true* shows card selection
* *false* skips to amount prompt

Since *preferReferencedReturns* is boolean, I analyzed both paths:

* If set to *false*: all cards get *requiresMatchingCard = false* making BBW's goal impossible
* If set to *true*: the result depends on the exclusion list

For BBW to achieve their goal, they would need:

* *preferReferencedReturns = true*
* Credit cards in *excludedCardTypes*
* This gives debit cards *true && true = true* (selection required)
* And credit cards *true && false = false* (auto-return)

However, BBW currently has debit cards in the exclusion list, which would produce opposite behavior if *preferReferencedReturns = true*.

Since I don't yet know BBW's current *preferReferencedReturns* setting, I need to confirm this value first before providing definitive configuration guidance, though it suggests they likely need to move credit cards to the exclusion list instead of debit cards.



----

*Where I Found This Logic:*

* *TenderReturnSummaryCalculator.java* - has the main logic and exclusion checking
* *TenderOptionsState.java* - makes the UI decision based on requiresMatchingCard
* *DefaultRequiresMatchingCardEndpoint.java* - returns the preferReferencedReturns value

Summary: When updating an existing promotion with a new effective date in the prm_assigned_promotion table, promotion cache building fails due to duplicate promotion keys, causing promotion calculation errors.
Description:
*Summary:*
 When updating an existing promotion with a new effective date in the {{prm_assigned_promotion}} table, promotion cache building fails due to duplicate promotion keys, causing promotion calculation errors.

*Impact:*
 High - No promotions are applied to transactions, severely affecting pricing and discount calculations at checkout.

*Detailed Description:*
 Upon inserting an updated promotion record with a new effective date into the {{prm_assigned_promotion}} table, the promotion cache build process throws a {{java.lang.IllegalStateException}} caused by duplicate keys for the same promotion ID during stream collection in {{CalculatePromotionEndpoint}}. This results in the failure of the promotion calculation service, leading to no promotions being applied during item scans or transactions. The error log indicates conflicting {{PromotionModel}} instances with identical keys, which prevents the system from correctly merging promotion data and impacts all sales operations relying on promotions.

Summary: Enable Home Office Users to Log In to Any Store in the Network
Description:
Currently, each POS user account in JumpMind is tied to a specific store location. This creates limitations for Home Office or Support users who need to remotely log in to different stores for troubleshooting, testing, or support purposes.

We would like to introduce a configuration enhancement to support a *“global” user type*, where the user’s assigned location can be set to a wildcard (e.g., “*”) or similar logic, allowing login access to any store in the network.

*Proposed Enhancement:*

* Add a user configuration option such as {{location = *}} (or “Global”) in the POS user setup.
* When this flag is set, the user should be allowed to authenticate at any store, without needing to be explicitly tied to that store’s location.
* Audit and security controls should still record the store ID from which the user logged in for traceability.

*Use Case:*
Home Office, Support, QA, or Integration teams often need to log into different stores’ POS systems for validation, troubleshooting, or testing purposes. The current restriction requires creating multiple user accounts, one per store -which is inefficient and difficult to maintain.

*Benefits:*

* Simplifies user management for Home Office and Support teams.
* Reduces the need for duplicate user accounts.
* Enables faster issue triage and testing across stores.

Summary: JM Transaction numbers are being re-used
Description:
Below is an example of what we are seeing. 

We identified a Missing Txn for 4724-012, Seq 2856 from Business Date Sep 20 (although technically Calendar Date Sept 21).

WE can see ONE instance of that Txn in Aptos Sales Audit (SA), and it is the original Till Reconciliation from when the Store was being closed.  We had a JSON Event from JumpMind which they Published when the original Txn happened, and our integration sent that to SA.

At some point later, JumpMind re-used the same Seq 2856 and subsequently over-wrote the Txn inside the JM DB with a new Return Txn.  That was not Published to a JSON for us to send to SA, because JM tracks which Seq #s have been Published already, so aa duplicate doesn't come across.  So the "version" of the Txn in JumpMind looks like a Return, and in SA it looks like a Till Reconciliation because they were in fact two different Txns.

In the attached log, we can see that the original Till Rec Txn appears in a function returning a Txn List in Line 67054 of the file.  Then in Line 68235 we see the "Next Sequence" number being assigned is in fact 2856 which was previously used.  And shortly later in Line 68249 we see the Seq # applied within a new Txn which is the Return that went missing (was never Published).

What we don't see in this log or the previous day's log was the actual completion of the original Txn (the Till Reconciliation) - we only see a reference to it in the "Search" function mentioned above.  And of course we know it DID exist at a point in time ot be Published in a JSON Event which we processed and sent to SA.

So we do believe this is proof of a Seq # being re-used, and we need to have this reviewed / resolved by the Jumpmind team.  Happy to join a call with them to review the findings as needed.

Summary: Tender Anytime - POS system to automatically apply pre-tendered data during the payment process and completely skip the Tender options screen  Sahitya Kareti raised this on 04/Aug/25 11:14 PM  Show
Description:
*Requirement Request/Description:*  
Implement functionality where, if a tender is pre-tendered as part of the "tender anytime" feature, the POS system automatically skips the tender options screen and uses the pre-tendered tender data for completing the transaction. The option to choose a different tender type or form of payment should not be available once pre-tendering is completed, except in cases where the payment is declined or the pre-tendered card does not have sufficient funds. In such cases, the system should return to the tender screen to allow the selection of an alternative payment method.

*Story Summary:*  
As a cashier, I want the POS system to automatically apply pre-tendered tender data during the payment process so that the tender options screen is bypassed and the transaction is completed using the pre-tendered data. (Note the tender options screen might be visible for a couple seconds but no button selection is required)  However, if the payment is declined or the tendered card has insufficient funds, the system should return to the tender screen for an alternate payment selection.

*Data Requirements:*

# The POS must bypass the tender options screen if pre-tendered data exists.
# The system should return to the tender screen only if the pre-tendered payment is declined or insufficient funds are detected.

*Tech Notes:*

*Acceptance Criteria:*

# If a tender is pre-tendered and the cashier selects Tender, the POS must skip the tender options screen and use the pre-tendered data to process the payment.
# If the pre-tendered payment is declined, the POS should return to the tender screen, allowing the cashier to select an alternative payment method.
# If the swiped GC has insufficient funds, the POS should debit the remaining balance and prompt for a different type of tender to cover the rest of the transaction.

       LEFT OUTER JOIN sls_void_trans VT

Summary: SearchCustomerEndpoint is not thread safe
Description: SearchCustomerEndpoint class is not thread safe and if multiple clients are connected to same service, could cause operation from one thread to impact other threads. Class level variables should be method parameters instead
Comments: 13/Oct/25 11:50 PM;712020:7a75bb53-325e-4baf-8fbf-140bffd5e3a3;[https://bathandbodyworks.atlassian.net/browse/POS-6895|https://bathandbodyworks.atlassian.net/browse/POS-6895]

14/Oct/25 10:18 AM;712020:2d65c990-e57a-4a01-bb8f-03917cc4a81f;Observations :
We observed that the searchMethod instance variable in the class SearchCustomerEndpoint is defined at the class level.

Since Spring beans are typically singletons, this variable is shared across concurrent requests. As a result, simultaneous calls to the searchCustomer() method could lead to one thread overwriting the value of searchMethod while another thread is still using it, potentially causing inconsistent or incorrect responses.

Summary: What is the purpose of Device Code Screen
Description:
We upgraded our dev env with JMC 250.0 release and as soon pos comes up we see new screen where it ask to enter the device code (please see attached). So we wanted to understand below:

# What is purpose of this screen?
# Whats codes need to entered here ?
# Is there a config to enable/disable this screen ?
# Is there any impact on BBW business (application/data flow)?
Comments: 15/Oct/25 8:22 AM;qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:16341683-ca79-4eb1-a5b2-4e3bd526be56;!Image.jpeg|thumbnail!

16/Oct/25 7:59 AM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;# What is purpose of this screen?
- The purpose is for IdP device authorization.  If IdP is enabled, you cannot skip the screen and have a successful login. The purpose for the code is to prevent unauthorized personalization for a particular device.
# Whats codes need to entered here ?
- If configured under IdP, you would simply enter a 6-digit code and all of the personalization would happen.
# Is there a config to enable/disable this screen ?
- No, it is not configurable and cannot be disabled.
# Is there any impact on BBW business (application/data flow)?
- No, if IdP is not configured you would just skip this screen.

16/Oct/25 8:00 AM;712020:1e31b905-2797-45c2-b5ac-e31ef7818f38;[~accountid:qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:16341683-ca79-4eb1-a5b2-4e3bd526be56] ,

# Is there a config to enable/disable this screen ?
- No, it is not configurable and cannot be disabled.
# Is there any impact on BBW business (application/data flow)?
- No, if IdP is not configured you would just skip this screen.

16/Oct/25 11:57 AM;qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:16341683-ca79-4eb1-a5b2-4e3bd526be56;Thanks for clarifying this.

I’d like to suggest making this screen configurable so that clients who do not use an Identity Provider (IdP) can have it disabled through configuration.

Since this screen is newly introduced, it has caused some confusion among users. Providing an option to enable or disable the IdP screen would help streamline the user experience and reduce unnecessary support inquiries for clients who don’t leverage IdP-based authentication.

{noformat}specificConfig:
  ops:
    strategy: REMOTE_FIRST
    endpoints:
      - path: /ops/openDevice
        strategy: LOCAL_ONLY
      - path: /ops/openTill
        strategy: LOCAL_ONLY
      - path: /ops/closeDevice
        strategy: REMOTE_FIRST     
      - path: /ops/closeTill

      - path: /ops/reconcileTill

      - path: /ops/tillStatus
        strategy: LOCAL_ONLY
      - path: /ops/deviceStatus
        strategy: REMOTE_FIRST      
      - path: /ops/storeStatus
        strategy: REMOTE_ONLY      {noformat}

So that should give that behavior: 

* /ops/deviceStatus: REMOTE_FIRST  # reg-001 sees all device statuses

Summary: BBW Request for Quick Loader to Upsert the item hierarchy when an Item gets reclassified
Description:
When an item is reclassified, a new entry is inserted into the {{itm_item_group_member}} table for the same {{item_id}} and {{category_type instead of updating the itm_group_id}}. This results in multiple records for the same item within a single category type.

The QuickLoader *delete feature* introduced in *JMC version 250.0* ([JMCH-1050|https://jumpmind.atlassian.net/browse/JMCH-1050]) does not delete the existing record when the same {{item_id}} and {{category_type}} already exist.

In the inbound message from SAP, we will get the information on what is updating but not what is to be deleted.

*Example:*

||item_id||item_group_id||category_type||
|28001050|0755|SUBCLASS|
|28001050|40070083|CLASS|
|28001050|{color:#ff5630}*40070098*{color}|{color:#ff5630}*CLASS*{color}|
|28001050|{color:#ff5630}*4062*{color}|{color:#ff5630}*SUBCLASS*{color}|

*Expected Behavior:*
When an item is reclassified, the {{item_group_id}} should be *updated* if a record already exists for the same {{item_id}} and {{category_type}}, instead of inserting a new record.

*Proposed Solution:*
Implement an *Upsert* feature in QuickLoader to:

* *Update* the existing entry if the {{item_id}} and {{category_type}} match. *Insert* a new record if no matching entry exists.

*Technical Consideration:*
The current primary key constraint for the {{item_group_member}} table is defined as:

{noformat}(item_id, item_group_id, category_type, tag_app_id, tag_business_unit_id, 
 tag_store_type, tag_brand, tag_device_type, tag_device_id, tag_country, tag_state)
{noformat}

If the constraint on {{item_group_id}} is removed, it would allow updates to the existing record (by {{item_id}} and {{category_type}}) instead of creating new entries for each group within the same category type.

We’re also open to other suggestions or recommendations for addressing this issue.

*Analysis & Fix*: Tried to pull the solution from the LLM (ChatGPT)

* Implement *debouncing* to limit prompt displays to only the last queued input in a short time window.
* *Clear the input queue* when the BbwCustomMaxQuantityActionHandler prompt is triggered to prevent multiple prompts.
* Introduce *throttling* for scanner input to ensure only one action is processed at a time.
* Reset the *input buffer* upon prompt display to prevent further queued actions from being processed.

This approach should address the issue of multiple prompt triggers due to rapid scanning.

{noformat}insert into sym_data (node_list, table_name, event_type, row_data, trigger_hist_id, channel_id, create_time)
select distinct node_list
     , 'SYM_NODE' as table_name
     , 'S' as event_type
     , concat('"insert into sym_data (node_list, table_name, event_type, row_data, trigger_hist_id, channel_id, create_time) values (''',child_node_list,''',''SYM_NODE'',''S'',''',row_data
             ,''',''',trigger_hist_id,''',''config'',current_timestamp)"') as row_data 
     , trigger_hist_id
     , 'config' as channel_id
     , current_timestamp as create_time
from
   (select distinct n.node_id as node_list
         , string_agg(cn.node_id,',' order by cn.node_id) as child_node_list
         , concat('delete from prm_reward_item where reward_item_id = ''''',ri1.reward_item_id,'''''') as row_data
         , (select trigger_hist_id from sym_trigger_hist where upper(trigger_id) = 'SYM_NODE' and inactive_time is null) as trigger_hist_id
    from prm_reward_item ri1
    inner join petco_promo_routing_reward_id rri
       on ri1.reward_id = rri.reward_id
    inner join sym_node n
       on (rri.tag_store_number = left(n.node_id, 5) or (1=1 and rri.tag_store_number = '*'))
      and n.node_id not like '%-%'
      and n.node_id not in ('00000')
    left outer join sym_node cn
       on (rri.tag_store_number = left(cn.node_id, 5) or (1=1 and rri.tag_store_number = '*' and n.node_id = left(cn.node_id, 5)))
      and cn.node_id like '%-%'
      and cn.node_id not in ('00000')
    where ri1.reward_id in (select reward_id from petco_cpg_prm_reward_item)
      and ri1.reward_item_id not in (select reward_item_id from petco_cpg_prm_reward_item)
    group by n.node_id, ri1.reward_item_id) T;
    {noformat}

17/Nov/25 9:04 AM;712020:2d65c990-e57a-4a01-bb8f-03917cc4a81f;Our observations based on Logs:
After reviewing both the Oct-14 and Oct-31 data from the store devices, we were able to identify why the Review Store Tills / Deposit Summary screen is showing the same amounts every day.

The values shown on the Deposit Summary screen come from special "control" records produced every day when a till is:Opened,Closed,Reconciled
These records tell the POS what the opening float and deposit amounts are for that day.

After reviewing the store’s data, we found that after October 14, the POS stopped generating these daily control records, even though associates were performing their normal open/close/count flow.
As a result:The screen kept showing the last valid amounts (from October 14) and Even though the actual deposit values in the database were correct

Inside the Oct-14 device logs, we found repeated errors during device startup:
Evidence #1 – Configuration loading failure
Error while parsing yml config value from database:
["openpos.ops.till.maxThreshold", "null"]

This means one of the till configuration fields was blank (null) in the database, and the POS could not load it properly.

Evidence #2 – Till assignment was failing
The logs also repeatedly show:

IOpsService.findTill()
IOpsService.getTillAssignment()

These operations normally confirm which till is assigned to the device.
Because a configuration error occurred, till assignment did not complete successfully.

When till assignment fails, the system cannot generate:OPEN_TILL,CLOSE_TILL,RECONCILE_TILL

These missing records are exactly what the Deposit Summary screen relies on.

Because the daily OPEN/CLOSE/RECONCILE control records were missing after Oct-14, the system had no new values to display.

So the UI continued to display the most recent valid set of control values, which were from: October 14 for all tills

This created the impression that every day had the same deposit and float amounts, even though the actual amounts you counted were correctly stored in the database.

28/Oct/25 3:04 PM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;After discussion with TVS today, here is what we _think_ might have happened. The promotions that are being seen as applying in their QE environment but are not displayed in Promote all had a status of DELETED. This status is reserved and applied only on promotions in Promote that are a DRAFT and have not been published to production. That said, I believe at one point, TVS had a workflow setup with a publish to QE step somewhere in between review steps. What I think may have happened is that a draft was submitted for review which went through the workflow and published to QE. Then somebody brought the promo back to draft and deleted the Draft for one reason or another and deleting that draft did not go through and clean up the promotion rows that were published to QE environment.

To test this out:

# Make sure the workflow has a publish to QE environment step.
# Create a draft and Submit for review/workflow pipeline.
# Make sure the draft promotion was published to the QE environment to test
# Send the promotion back to Draft
# Delete the draft promotion
# Check if the promotion is still existing on QE environment (if it is, this is your bug and a fix is needed to ensure that deleting a draft cleans up/deletes the promotion from QE to any publish to QE steps that may have run).

Summary: US Cash is increased at end of day if a CASH DOWN is performed during the day
Description:
US Cash is being increased by the amount of a cash down done during the day.  This bug was found on the RCL project.

Steps to reproduce:

# Open the store, register and till and make note of the till amount
# Perform enough CASH transactions including one for US CASH that will flag the cash limit for the till exceeding amount message
# Perform a CASH DOWN transaction
# Perform more cash transactions
# Close and reconcile the till making note of the funds
# Close the register
# Close the store and reconcile the till.

EXPECTED RESULT: The amount of cash to be sent to the bank for CDN funds should include the amount removed from the till. The amount of cash to be sent to the bank for US funds should only include the amount from the one transaction.

ACTUAL RESULT: The amount of cash to be sent to the bank for US funds includes the amount removed from the till even though it is already included in the CDN funds.

Summary: Customer double charged: Receiving null response from Aurus
Description:
We are seeing socket disconnection *without receiving any bytes* at all from Aurus. In this case, JMC does not know what happened on Aurus side, so it proceeds as a failure. Before we used to get *some bytes* response from Aurus, then the socket (-1 bytes) disconnects. Here, JMC fixed it in base so that the already received bytes are not ignored, and the response is handled properly - this was done in JMCH-1049 

Here, Aurus is recommending we send a CancelLastTrans request to handle these scenarios:

# null response from Aurus
# timeout response from Aurus
# timeout response triggered by JMC POS when nothing is received from Aurus

Adyen successfully processed the Discover (or Visa) payment —
The logs confirm a “Response: SUCCESS” from Adyen at 15:15:25.240, with full transaction details (AID, TID, PSP Reference, etc.).

POS began its finalization process —
Immediately after that, POS invoked FinalizeTendering and called ITransMgmtService.finalizeSaleSession() at 15:15:25.841, followed by TransCompleteEvent indicating the transaction was marked COMPLETED internally.

However, after a short delay (~10 sec), a cancel signal was triggered —

This indicates that the MPOS → POS callback (acknowledging the completed tender) did not reach in time, and the timeout window expired.

POS interpreted the delay as a timeout and reopened the Tender screen, automatically canceling the session.
Because the Adyen completion occurred milliseconds before the timeout threshold, POS had already moved to a “cancel flow” state when the callback response arrived.

Claude Response: 

*Yes, it's theoretically possible but MUCH less likely.* Let me explain the scenarios where Local API could hit this:

h2. Scenarios Where Local API Could Hit the Same Issue

h3. Scenario 1: Network Interruption During Response

*The vulnerable window:*

{noformat}1. POS → Terminal: "Authorize $100" (request sent successfully)
2. Terminal → Payment Processor: Authorization request
3. Processor → Terminal: "Approved" (authorization succeeds)
4. Terminal → POS: "Approved" response starts sending...
5. ❌ NETWORK CABLE UNPLUGGED or WiFi drops ❌
6. POS: ConnectTimeoutException - never received response
7. Terminal: Has successful authorization in memory{noformat}

*With the ServiceID reuse bug:*

* POS tries to call {{getTransactionStatusRequest()}} with same ServiceID
* Adyen returns "Repeated DB message"
* POS can't determine transaction succeeded
* Customer charged, POS shows error

*Why this is rare in Local API:*

* The response transmission takes *milliseconds* on local network
* The vulnerable window is ~10-50ms
* Cable would need to be unplugged at the exact moment
* WiFi dropout would need to occur in that tiny window

h3. Scenario 2: Terminal or POS Process Crash

*The vulnerable window:*

{noformat}1. POS → Terminal: "Authorize $100"
2. Terminal processes authorization (takes 2-5 seconds)
3. ✅ Authorization succeeds on Terminal
4. ❌ POS process crashes before receiving response ❌
   OR
4. ❌ Terminal crashes after authorizing but before sending response ❌{noformat}

*This would cause the same split-brain state:*

* Authorization completed on terminal/processor
* POS never got the response
* Recovery with ServiceID reuse would fail

*Why this is rare:*

* Process crashes are uncommon
* Would need to happen in the 2-5 second processing window

h3. Scenario 3: Local Network Congestion/Packet Loss

*The vulnerable window:*

{noformat}1. POS sends authorization request (gets through)
2. Terminal authorizes successfully
3. Terminal sends response packet(s)
4. ❌ Network switch drops packets due to congestion ❌
5. POS timeout expires waiting for response{noformat}

*With TCP/IP this is extremely rare because:*

* TCP has built-in retransmission
* Local network switches rarely drop packets
* Even with congestion, TCP will retry
* Would need severe network failure

h3. Scenario 4: Firewall/Switch Configuration Issue

*Could happen if:*

{noformat}1. Firewall allows outbound request (POS → Terminal)
2. Authorization succeeds on terminal
3. Firewall blocks inbound response (Terminal → POS)
4. POS times out waiting for response{noformat}

*Why this is rare:*

* Misconfiguration usually blocks both directions
* Would be caught immediately during testing
* If response blocked, subsequent requests also blocked (issue obvious)

h2. Probability Comparison

Let me create a rough probability estimate:

h3. Cloud API (Based on JMCH-1341 Evidence)

*Timeout occurrence probability:*

* Network latency: 200-400ms per hop × 3 hops = 600-1200ms baseline
* Discover processing: +30-60 seconds
* Internet variability: High
* *Estimated timeout rate: 1-5% of Discover transactions*

*Recovery failure due to ServiceID bug:* 100% (always fails)

*Result: ~1-5% of Discover transactions have the issue*

h3. Local API

*Timeout occurrence probability:*

* Network latency: 10-50ms (local network)
* Processing time: 2-5 seconds (same as Cloud)
* Vulnerable window: ~50ms during response transmission
* Cable/WiFi failure during 50ms window: ~0.001%
* Process crash during 2-5s window: ~0.01%
* Network congestion severe enough: ~0.001%
* *Estimated timeout rate: ~0.01-0.02% of transactions*

*Recovery failure due to ServiceID bug:* 100% (same bug exists)

*Result: ~0.01-0.02% of transactions have the issue*

h2. The Math

*Cloud API:* 1-5% timeout rate × 100% recovery failure = *1-5% visible to customers*

*Local API:* 0.01-0.02% timeout rate × 100% recovery failure = *0.01-0.02% visible to customers*

*Cloud API is roughly 100-500x more likely to hit this issue.*

h2. Why You Haven't Heard From Local API Clients

With a 0.01-0.02% occurrence rate:

* *10,000 transactions* = 1-2 occurrences
* Might be dismissed as "one-off glitch"
* Attributed to user error or hardware failure
* Not enough volume to establish a pattern

With a 1-5% occurrence rate (Cloud API):

* *10,000 transactions* = 100-500 occurrences
* *Impossible to ignore* - clear pattern
* Especially visible at pop-up shops with high Discover usage
* Gets escalated to support immediately

h2. Conclusion

*Yes, Local API can hit this scenario with the current code*, but:

# *It's ~100-500x less likely* due to network architecture
# *When it does happen*, it's rare enough to not establish a pattern
# *The same ServiceID reuse bug exists* in both paths
# *Your fix will benefit both*, but Cloud API benefits much more since it hits the code path constantly

*The bug is a "code defect" that affects both implementations, but it's a "production crisis" only for Cloud API due to frequency.*

This is actually good news for your fix - *once you fix the ServiceID reuse bug, both Local API and Cloud API will be more robust*, but Cloud API will go from "frequently broken" to "occasionally resilient."

12/Jan/26 7:14 AM;712020:877ebe8a-e44a-419d-b0bd-b385e6a816f3;Duplicate payloads were sent for the same transaction due to publishing at two different points in the transaction lifecycle.

* During transaction processing, an exception occurred:
{{org.joda.money.IllegalCurrencyException: Unknown currency 'QSD'}} while inserting into {{sls_trans_user_action}}.
* At the time of this exception, JMC published the transaction in an *intermediate state*, resulting in the *first payload* with:
** {{transStatusCode = ORPHANED}}
** Minimal / incomplete transaction data
** {{appVersion = 0}}
* After the transaction flow recovered and completed, JMC published the transaction *again*, generating the *second payload* with:
** {{transStatusCode = CANCELLED}}
** Fully populated line items, taxes, totals, and resolved currency ({{USD}})
** Correct application version

Since there is no suppression or rollback of the initial publish on error, both the *partial (ORPHANED)* and *final (CANCELLED)* payloads were sent downstream, resulting in duplicate messages for the same transaction sequence.

Summary: Refund amount is not correct when performing Full Receipted Return from Sale includes $0.00 items after applying Welcome offer and Loyalty Reward.
Description:
we have a discount reward and a free item reward. When both are applied in same sale, returning all the items result in different total than the sale. 

 Issue occurs when the transaction includes prorated discounts and multiple coupons. 

+*RootCause:*+

*Whenever the transaction involves prorated discount calculation with free item, the extendedDiscountAmount is skipping one of the priceModifierLine item entry.*

(see image 6d21)

In the above table, 1.12 got  skipped in the calculation.

*While returning entries with 10 qty each having list price as 10*

{color:#ff5630}*In the first 2 iteration,  discountAmount = (10+1.11* 2 )=22.22,*{color}

{color:#ff5630}*In the remaining iteration,*{color}{color:#ff5630} {color}{color:#ff5630}*discountAmount=1.11*6=6.66.*{color}

{color:#ff5630}*totalDiscountAmount=28.88*{color}

{color:#ff5630}*TotalPrice = 100-28.88=71.12*{color}

 *1.12 is skipped in the calculation and resulting in calculating the free items twice.*

*Upon updating 1.12 to 1.11 → return amount calculated correctly.*

(see image 6e9d)

+*Issue Identified in the below class*+

The extendedDiscount Amount calculation happening within the method *AddReturnToTransEndpoint*.*getExtendedDiscountedAmountWithPromosForReceiptedReturnItem()* is incorrect.

We are calculating the DiscountAmount based on the price modifiers entry present in the sls_retail_line_item_price_mod table and while iterating through the sorted price_modifier_list based on the mod_amount in desc, the exact quanity_index match between return price modifier list and original price_modifer_list causes a missing discount calculation for one of the price modifier entry.

(see image 4a01)

16/Jan/26 3:53 PM;712020:8b234d7e-962d-4107-8fb4-b2943c64dde2;h2. Resolution Analysis Complete

*Root Cause Confirmed:* The SwipeOnDevice button is disabled by default in the CTX_BUTTON table (ENABLED='0'), which prevents the primary action button from appearing on the gift card scan screen. When this button is disabled, the code in ScanGiftCardState.java (lines 122-126) does not set an action button, and the secondary action button ("Next") is not properly rendered on mobile devices.

*Evidence from Code Analysis:*
* ScanGiftCardState.java line 122-126 shows the conditional logic that only sets the action button when SwipeOnDevice is enabled
* post_00_ctx-button.csv lines 113-114 confirm SwipeOnDevice buttons have ENABLED='0' for both 'sale.transaction.giftCard' and 'tender.tenderOptions.giftCard' button groups
* The secondary action button is set at line 106, but when no primary action button exists, the UI may not render the secondary button correctly on mobile

*Confidence Level:* 95%

----

h2. Recommended Resolution

*Immediate Fix (Database Configuration):*
\{code:sql}
UPDATE CTX_BUTTON 
SET ENABLED = 1 
WHERE BUTTON_ID = 'SwipeOnDevice' 
AND BUTTON_GROUP_ID IN ('sale.transaction.giftCard', 'tender.tenderOptions.giftCard');
\{code}

*Verification Query:*
\{code:sql}
SELECT BUTTON_GROUP_ID, BUTTON_ID, ENABLED 
FROM CTX_BUTTON 
WHERE BUTTON_ID = 'SwipeOnDevice';
\{code}

*Steps:*
# Connect to the database
# Execute the UPDATE statement above
# Verify the update with the SELECT query
# Restart POS client application to reload button configuration
# Test gift card balance inquiry with manual entry and scan on mobile device

----

h2. Long-term Code Fix Recommended

A PR should be created to update the foundation data CSV to enable SwipeOnDevice by default, and optionally add graceful degradation in ScanGiftCardState.java to show the Next button as primary when SwipeOnDevice is disabled.

10/Nov/25 5:37 PM;712020:0b3de8b9-fd84-40a7-a9ca-77e86f66a0b0;What I'm seeing is that when responses for XCC and Aurus take longer than JMC is configured for, a BackgroundTransactionManagerUpdater thread is spawned to wait for a response, which allows another item to be scanned.  If multiple items are scanned in succession that take longer than configured, then more threads are spawned in a waiting state that continue to take up system resources.  So the root cause may not necessarily be the performance of the this particular thread, but the long running responses combined with the multiple waiting threads causing spikes in system resource utilization.

Summary: Provide replication confirmation or flags for transactions from Fixed → BO and Fixed → CO
Description:
We are setting up monitoring for transaction replication and need to track when transactions are successfully replicated across systems. Specifically, we’d like:

# A flag or indicator in the system that shows a transaction has been successfully replicated from *Fixed to Business Unit (BU)*.
# A flag or indicator that confirms a transaction has been replicated from *BU to Central Unit (CO)*.

This information will help us implement a reliable monitoring mechanism to proactively detect replication issues and ensure smooth data flow across systems.

We would like to highlight that in our legacy ORPOS implementation, there is already a mechanism at the store database level to track whether a transaction has been successfully replicated to the Central Office. This information is critical for several dependent processes, such as RTLog generation, cross-store returns, reconciliation, and other key reports and validations that rely on complete and accurate transaction replication status.

Given these dependencies and the operational importance of knowing the replication state, we would like to request that a similar capability be considered within the base product itself. Having a system-driven flag or indicator to track replication status (from Store to Central) would enable proactive monitoring, improve data consistency, and reduce the need for custom solutions.

This enhancement would greatly help in ensuring data integrity across distributed environments and streamline downstream business processes that depend on replicated transactions.

Your process would have to run multiple times to get the counts as not all stores will be closed at the same time and then what if some registers are offline.  You have to consider there are many moving parts when you do your comparisons as data is trickling in as it happens and potentially stores in different time zones.
