02/Feb/26 11:49 AM;712020:ad7b5cf3-9cd3-4ec8-a07c-c53367ad4328;h1. AI Investigation Summary

h2. Root Cause Analysis

The license key expired error across all registers is caused by a *database-stored license key configuration that is incorrect or expired*, which overrides the correct YML file configuration due to configuration precedence rules.

*Evidence:*

* The {{ContextPropertySource}} loads configuration from the {{ctx_config}} database table and is registered with highest precedence in Spring's property source chain
* Database values take priority over YML file values, meaning an incorrect/expired license key in the database will be used even if the YML has the correct value
* Cache clearing alone does not resolve the issue because the cache is repopulated from the database, which still contains the incorrect value
* The system lacks automatic cache eviction configuration for the {{ctx_config}} table, requiring manual intervention when license configuration is updated via SymmetricDS replication

h2. Affected Components

* {{ContextPropertySourceInitializer}} - Registers database property source with highest precedence
* {{ContextPropertySource}} - Loads config from ctx_config table
* {{ConfigManager}} / {{ConfigHelper}} - Configuration retrieval with caching
* {{LicenseKeyChecker}} - Validates license key
* {{ContextRepository}} - Database access for configuration (uses {{contextConfig}} cache)

Advantages of Separate Listeners

||Advantage||Benefit||
|*Single Responsibility Principle*|Each listener has one clear job|
|*Independent Failure Handling*|If tender persistence fails, line item persistence still runs|
|*Easier Testing*|Test each concern in isolation|
|*Flexible Configuration*|Enable/disable independently via Spring profiles|
|*Clear Ownership*|Different teams can own different listeners|
|*Better Logging*|Isolated log messages per concern|
|*Follows JMC Patterns*|Matches how JMC organizes its own listeners|
|*Future Extensibility*|Easy to add more listeners for new custom tables|
|*Reduced Complexity*|Each class is simpler and easier to understand|

Error Handling Best Practices

# *Never rethrow exceptions* - Custom persistence failures should NOT block transaction completion
# *Log at appropriate levels* - ERROR for failures, INFO for success, DEBUG for details
# *Include transaction key* - Always log transaction key for traceability
# *Consider alerting* - Set up monitoring for persistence failures
# *Graceful degradation* - Transaction should complete even if custom persistence fails

Use Separate Listeners When:

* The processing serves different functional domains (for example, tender analytics versus line-item reporting)
* Each listener requires different repositories or dependencies
* Failure isolation is important, so an issue in one area does not impact the other
* You need the ability to enable or disable the functionality independently
* The components are owned or maintained by different teams or modules
* The logic involves distinct validation or transformation rules

Use a Single Consolidated Listener When:

* The data is tightly coupled and follows the same processing lifecycle
* Strict transactional consistency is required across all custom tables
* All persistence relies on the same repositories and dependencies
* The use case is simple and involves minimal processing logic

*Documentation:* [https://commerce-docs.jumpmind.com/Implementors/Extending/Finalizers.html|https://commerce-docs.jumpmind.com/Implementors/Extending/Finalizers.html]

Summary: Questions related to All registers and stores experienced “License key expired” errors on POS.
Description:
# There are *multiple license keys*, with the latest dated *11/25*, expiring *Feb 1*.
#* Is the code using *Effective Start Time* to determine the active/latest key?
#* Why does db have multiple entries for license keys
#* How are these license keys being inserted into the db? Is there a separate process for this

!image-20260203-112438.png|width=1075,height=283,alt="image-20260203-112438.png"!

# Why did some stores encounter license errors while others did not, despite:
#* Similar reboot cycles
#* Same system time
# How can we identify when a license key is approaching expiration?
#* Is there a way to get *notified prior to expiry*?
# {{clearAllCaches}} does not appear to be working.
#* What are the next steps to get this fixed before the next release?
#* Does the API return a success/failure response?
Comments:
03/Feb/26 1:14 PM;712020:ad7b5cf3-9cd3-4ec8-a07c-c53367ad4328;h1. AI Investigation Summary

h2. Root Cause Analysis

The license key expiration issue affecting all registers and stores is caused by a *combination of two factors*:

# *Incorrect License Key Selection Logic*: The {{configsByTag}} query in {{ctx-query.yml}} orders results by {{effective_start_time desc}}, which selects the license key with the *most recent start time* rather than the one with the *furthest expiration date*. When multiple license keys exist in the database (9+ entries found), the system may select an expired or soon-to-expire key instead of the valid one.

# *Cache Invalidation Not Fully Effective*: The {{ClearAllCachesEndpoint}} clears Spring CacheManager caches, but the {{ConfigHelper.getAllConfigs()}} method uses {{@Cacheable(value = "contextConfig")}} annotation. While the cache clearing should work, the timing of cache refresh combined with the wrong key selection means stores that rebooted at different times loaded different license keys.

*Evidence:*

* Query ordering in {{ctx-query.yml}} line 160: {{orderBy: config_name, effective_start_time desc}}
* Multiple license key entries in {{ctx_config}} table with same {{config_name='license.key'}} and {{enabled=1}}
* {{ConfigHelper.java}} line 72: {{@Cacheable(value = "contextConfig")}} on {{getAllConfigs()}} method
* {{GetLicenseKeyEndpoint.java}} line 21: Uses {{configManager.getString("license.key", "")}} which relies on the flawed selection logic

h2. Affected Components

* {{headless/services/context/src/main/resources/ctx-query.yml}} - Query ordering logic
* {{headless/services/context/src/main/java/org/jumpmind/pos/context/service/ConfigHelper.java}} - Caching layer
* {{headless/services/context/src/main/java/org/jumpmind/pos/context/service/GetLicenseKeyEndpoint.java}} - License key retrieval
* {{headless/core/service-core/src/main/java/org/jumpmind/pos/service/ClearAllCachesEndpoint.java}} - Cache clearing
* {{headless/services/context/src/main/java/org/jumpmind/pos/context/service/ConfigManager.java}} - Config management

h2. Recommended Fix

h3. Immediate Workaround (Database Cleanup)

*Step 1: Identify the correct license key*

{code:sql}-- Run this query to see all license keys and their expiration dates
SELECT 
  sequence_number,
  config_name,
  config_value,
  effective_start_time,
  effective_end_time,
  enabled
FROM ctx_config 
WHERE config_name = 'license.key' 
  AND (enabled IS NULL OR enabled = 1)
ORDER BY 
  CASE WHEN effective_end_time IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END DESC,
  effective_end_time DESC NULLS LAST;{code}

*Step 2: Disable all license keys except the one with the furthest expiration*

{code:sql}-- First, identify the sequence_number of the best key from Step 1
-- Then disable all others:
UPDATE ctx_config 
SET enabled = 0 
WHERE config_name = 'license.key' 
  AND sequence_number != <BEST_SEQUENCE_NUMBER>;{code}

*Step 3: Clear caches and restart*

{code:bash}# Call the clear caches API
curl -X POST https://<server>/api/admin/clearAllCaches

# If issues persist, restart POS servers{code}

h3. Long-term Code Fix (Recommended)

*Option A: Modify Query Ordering (Low Risk)*

File: {{headless/services/context/src/main/resources/ctx-query.yml}}

Change line 160 from:

{code:yaml}orderBy: config_name, effective_start_time desc{code}

To:

{code:yaml}orderBy: config_name, effective_end_time desc NULLS FIRST, effective_start_time desc{code}

This ensures that when multiple configs exist with the same name, the one with the furthest expiration (or NULL = never expires) is selected first.

*Option B: Add License-Specific Selection Logic (More Targeted)*

Add a new method to {{ConfigManager.java}} specifically for license key retrieval:

{code:java}// File: headless/services/context/src/main/java/org/jumpmind/pos/context/service/ConfigManager.java

public String getLicenseKey() {
    DeviceModel device = getConfigDevice();
    List<Config> licenseKeys = configHelper.getAllConfigs(device.getTags())
        .stream()
        .filter(c -> c.getConfigName().equals("license.key"))
        .collect(Collectors.toList());
    
    if (licenseKeys.isEmpty()) {
        return env.getProperty("license.key", "");
    }
    
    // Select key with furthest expiration (NULL = never expires)
    Config selectedKey = licenseKeys.stream()
        .max(Comparator.comparing(
            c -> c.getEffectiveEndTime() != null ? c.getEffectiveEndTime() : LocalDateTime.MAX,
            Comparator.nullsFirst(Comparator.naturalOrder())
        ))
        .orElse(licenseKeys.get(0));
    
    if (licenseKeys.size() > 1) {
        log.warn("Multiple active license keys found ({}). Selected key expiring: {}", 
            licenseKeys.size(), selectedKey.getEffectiveEndTime());
    }
    
    return selectedKey.getConfigValue();
}{code}

Then update {{GetLicenseKeyEndpoint.java}} line 21:

{code:java}// Change from:
String licenseKeyConfig = configManager.getString("license.key", "");

// To:
String licenseKeyConfig = configManager.getLicenseKey();{code}

h2. Answers to Customer Questions

# *Is the code using Effective Start Time to determine the active/latest key?*

   - Yes, the query orders by {{effective_start_time desc}}, which selects the most recently started key, not the one with the longest validity.

# *Why does db have multiple entries for license keys?*

   - License keys are stored as config entries. When new keys are added, old ones are not automatically disabled. This is by design for other configs but problematic for license keys.

# *How are license keys being inserted into the db?*

   - License keys are inserted via the {{SaveConfigEndpoint}} API or through data synchronization. There's no automatic cleanup of old keys.

# *Why did some stores encounter license errors while others did not?*

   - Race condition: Stores that rebooted or cleared cache at different times may have loaded different license keys based on which key had the most recent {{effective_start_time}} at that moment.

# *How can we identify when a license key is approaching expiration?*

   - Currently there's no built-in notification. Recommend adding a scheduled job to check {{effective_end_time}} and alert when within 30 days of expiration.

# *Does clearAllCaches return a success/failure response?*

   - The endpoint returns void (HTTP 200 on success). It does clear the {{contextConfig}} cache, but the underlying issue is the selection logic, not the cache clearing.

h2. Testing Steps

# Run the database query to verify only one enabled license key exists
# Call {{GET /api/context/licenseKey}} and verify the correct key is returned
# Restart a POS device and verify it connects without license errors
# Check logs for any "License key expired" errors

h2. Confidence Level

*High* (0.92) - Root cause clearly identified in code analysis. Query ordering logic confirmed in {{ctx-query.yml}}. Multiple contributing factors documented with code evidence.

Summary: Refactor sls_return_tender and returnAmountAvailable and returnAmountAvailable/set endpoints to keep track of history, not just total
Description:
Currently we are seeing an issue in prod where stores go offline sometimes (network issues or dropped packets or whatever other reasons) and we are seeing the sls_return_tender data get written in business unit database instead of central. However, as per discussions with John Varcho, this is by design to mitigate complicated offline/online scenarios causing the central db to end up with a wrong total. 

Currently this table looks like this
session_identifier            amount_tendered     amount_remaining
124295413758186897	22.540	                  0.000

on a given session identifier, just the total tendered, and remaining total is kept track. 

The problem we see is that with this approach the last record to update is deemed “truth” which in race conditions might not be correct.

Instead of just tracking the total remaining, if each line also had transaction details or something like that and their individual totals on that session, then you can just combine all and remove from amount_tendered to get remaining. This way, even if some store has offline issues, we can replicate that up to central and just combining will give us actual true amount remaining. 

Set to High as its impacting prod stores and customer expierience

* *SyncTriggersJob*: Scheduled job that syncs triggers (runs at midnight by default)
* *sym_trigger / sym_trigger_router*: Configuration tables that replicate immediately
* *sym_trigger_hist*: Maintains trigger creation history and error states

WHERE th.error_message LIKE '%Table not found%'

ORDER BY th.create_time DESC;{code}

*Step 2: Force Trigger Regeneration*

h2. Root Cause Analysis

The {{upt_mgmt_installation}} table is *designed to track Auto Updater deployments*, but it requires the *update-mgmt microservice* to be deployed and the bootstrap service to be configured with the {{auto-update.url}} property. Without this configuration, the POS devices cannot report their installation status to the centralized update management server.

*Evidence:*

* Code analysis confirms {{UpdateClientService.reportAutoUpdateResults()}} sends installation status to {{bootstrapProperties.getAutoUpdateUrl() + "/api/update/report/install"}}
* The {{BootstrapProperties.isFullyProvisioned()}} method requires {{auto-update.url}} to be set
* Bootstrap logs show no errors related to update reporting, suggesting the feature is simply not configured (not failing)
* The {{sls_trans}} table correctly shows version 243.1.35, confirming the Auto Updater deployment itself succeeded
* This is an on-prem deployment that likely does not have the update-mgmt microservice deployed

h2. Affected Components

* {{UpdateClientService.java}} - Reports installation status to update server
* {{BootstrapProperties.java}} - Contains {{auto-update.url}} configuration
* {{ReportInstallStatusEndpoint.java}} - Server-side endpoint that writes to {{upt_mgmt_installation}}
* {{InstallationModel.java}} - Maps to {{upt_mgmt_installation}} table
* {{application-<service>-bootstrap.properties}} - Configuration file on POS devices

h2. Recommended Fix

h3. Option 1: Immediate Workaround - Use Alternative Tracking Methods (Recommended for Now)

Since the update-mgmt server is not deployed, use the {{sls_trans}} table to track deployed versions:

{code:sql}-- Query to track versions by store from transaction data
SELECT 
  business_unit_id,
  app_version,
  MIN(create_time) as first_seen,
  MAX(create_time) as last_seen,
  COUNT(*) as transaction_count
FROM sls_trans
WHERE create_time >= '2026-02-01'
GROUP BY business_unit_id, app_version
ORDER BY business_unit_id, first_seen DESC;{code}

Alternatively, check the {{microservice}} table:

{code:sql}SELECT installation_id, current_version, last_update_time 
FROM microservice 
WHERE installation_id LIKE '60318%'
ORDER BY installation_id;{code}

h3. Option 2: Enable Full Deployment Tracking (Long-term Solution)

To enable the {{upt_mgmt_installation}} table tracking:

*Step 1:* Deploy the update-mgmt microservice on a central server

* This microservice provides the {{/api/update/report/install}} and {{/api/update/report/heartbeat}} endpoints
* Configure database connection for the {{upt_mgmt}} schema
* Ensure firewall rules allow POS devices to connect

*Step 2:* Configure each POS device's bootstrap properties

Edit {{application-<service>-bootstrap.properties}} in the work directory (typically {{C:\Jumpmind\point-of-sale}}):

{noformat}# Add these properties to enable update tracking
auto-update.url=http://<update-mgmt-server-host>:<port>
auto-update.package-name=commerce
openpos.businessunitId=<store-id>
openpos.installationId=<device-id>{noformat}

*Step 3:* Restart the bootstrap service on each POS device

*Step 4:* Future deployments will automatically report to {{upt_mgmt_installation}}

h3. Important Notes

* Historical deployments (including 243.1.35) will *not* be retroactively tracked
* The update-mgmt microservice is typically used for cloud deployments; on-prem customers may need to deploy it separately
* Contact Jumpmind for guidance on deploying the update-mgmt microservice for on-prem environments

Summary: Commerce Central Server v250.2.1 - Spring Security Filter Chain Conflict Preventing Application Startup in SIT Environment
Description:
Problem Summary:

  The Commerce Central Server application is failing to start due to a Spring Security configuration conflict. The application encounters an UnreachableFilterChainException during startup, preventing the service from becoming available.



  Root Cause:

  Two Spring Security filter chains are configured to handle "any request", creating a conflict:

# NoSecurityConfig.class → bean name: filterChain

# SecurityConfig.class → bean name: securityFilterChain

Causing Spring Security to be unable to determine precedence, resulting in application startup failure.

  Error Details:

  org.springframework.security.web.UnreachableFilterChainException: A filter chain that matches any request [DefaultSecurityFilterChain defined as 'filterChain' in [class path resource [org/jumpmind/idp/NoSecurityConfig.class]] matching [any request]] has already been configured, which means that this filter chain [DefaultSecurityFilterChain defined as 'securityFilterChain' in [class path resource [org/jumpmind/commerce/central/server/auth/SecurityConfig.class]] matching [any request]] will never get invoked.

h3. Primary Solution: Add securityMatcher to NoSecurityConfig (Recommended)

Modify {{NoSecurityConfig.java}} to restrict its filter chain scope to actuator/health endpoints only, allowing other SecurityFilterChain beans to handle application requests.

*File:* {{headless/core/idp-client/src/main/java/org/jumpmind/idp/NoSecurityConfig.java}}

{code:java}package org.jumpmind.idp;

import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.condition.ConditionalOnMissingBean;
import org.springframework.boot.autoconfigure.condition.ConditionalOnProperty;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Bean;
import org.springframework.context.annotation.Configuration;
import org.springframework.core.annotation.Order;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.builders.HttpSecurity;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.configurers.AbstractHttpConfigurer;
import org.springframework.security.config.annotation.web.configurers.HeadersConfigurer;
import org.springframework.security.web.SecurityFilterChain;

@Configuration
@ConditionalOnProperty(prefix = "secured.idp", name = "enabled", havingValue = "false", matchIfMissing = true)
public class NoSecurityConfig {

    @Bean
    @ConditionalOnMissingBean
    public SecurityFilterChain filterChain(HttpSecurity http) throws Exception {
        return http
                .securityMatcher("/actuator/**", "/health", "/health/**")  // ADD THIS LINE
                .csrf(AbstractHttpConfigurer::disable)
                .authorizeHttpRequests(auth -> auth.anyRequest().permitAll())
                .headers(headers -> headers.frameOptions(HeadersConfigurer.FrameOptionsConfig::sameOrigin))
                .build();

To cancel pending reloads that haven't been picked up yet:

First, check what reload channel is configured for the affected triggers:

{noformat}  SELECT trigger_id, source_table_name, channel_id, reload_channel_id
  FROM sym_trigger
  WHERE source_table_name IN ('sls_order');{noformat}

Use whatever reload_channel_id comes back in the queries below. The default is typically 'reload' but may differ.

Remove any reload requests that are still queued and haven't been processed:

{noformat}  SELECT * FROM sym_table_reload_request WHERE processed = 0;{noformat}

If those look like the ones you want to cancel:

{noformat}  DELETE FROM sym_table_reload_request WHERE processed = 0;{noformat}

Then check for any reload batches sitting in NE (not yet sent) status. The load_flag column indicates whether a batch is part of a reload:

{noformat}  SELECT batch_id, node_id, channel_id, status, create_time
  FROM sym_outgoing_batch
  WHERE status = 'NE'
    AND load_flag = 1
  ORDER BY batch_id DESC;{noformat}

Review those results, and if they match the reloads you want to cancel:

{noformat}  UPDATE sym_outgoing_batch
  SET status = 'IG'
  WHERE status = 'NE'
    AND load_flag = 1;{noformat}

Anything already mid-flight (status LD or SE) will need to finish on its own. This only cancels the ones that haven't started yet.

Analysis of logs confirms that a single gift card scan is triggering multiple actions, leading to concurrent payment requests and device conflicts.

# The same barcode is received multiple times within milliseconds:

# Cancel/CloseTransaction is triggered while another request is active:
#* Multiple {{CloseTransactionRequest}} sent
#* {{SocketException: Socket closed}}
#* {{PaymentMessagingException}} logged

*Conclusion (Log-Based):*
A single scan is generating multiple {{Scan}} and {{CheckForCardData}} actions. This results in concurrent Aurus requests, latch conflicts ({{CCT IS BUSY}}), forced CloseTransaction calls, socket closures, and payment exceptions.

This behavior explains:

* Double activation attempts (“gift card already activated”)
* GC issue failures
* POS freezing during GC operations

*What the logs show is a state/flow mismatch caused by an extra* {{CheckForCardData}} *action arriving after the ScanGiftCard flow has already exited.*

h4. Evidence chain from the logs:

# *POS is in gift-card scan flow and receives* {{CheckForCardData}} *with the scanned card data.*
The device sends the scan action: {{{"name":"CheckForCardData","data":{"data":"6006496114999903645"},"type":"Dialog","doNotBlockForResponse":false}}} while the UI is in the GiftCardScan prompt. 2026-02-27 115133

{{[StateManager] Unexpected action "CheckForCardData". Either no @ActionHandler ...PostTenderAuthorizeGiftCardState.onCheckForCardData()... or no withTransition("CheckForCardData"...) defined in the "GiftCardPostTenderAuthorizationFlow" flow config.}} 2026-02-27 115133

13/Feb/26 2:19 PM;712020:03eb0e30-3eea-4831-9533-05d046229d05;Hi [~accountid:qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:6613b0b5-f97d-4063-8c75-2271021f3b69]  - thank you for the .yml files! I see you have {{maxThreshold: 900}} configured in {{application-base.yml}}, but based on your reproduction steps (reducing till cash below the float amount), it looks like you'd also need a {{minThreshold}} configured to trigger a notification in that specific scenario.

Add this in your {{application-base.yml}} , near the {{maxThreshold}} config, like so:

{noformat}  openpos:
    ops:
      till:
        minThreshold: 400{noformat}

(Adjust the value to whatever minimum cash amount should trigger an alert.)



Additionally, the +notify service+ isn't routed to the BU on fixed registers, so when a threshold notification gets created on the BU, the register can't see it. In your {{application-fixed.yml}}, please try adding this:

{noformat}  openpos:
    services:
      specificConfig:
        notify:
          strategy: REMOTE_FIRST
          profileIds:
            - remote_businessunit{noformat}

This ensures that when the home screen queries for notifications, it reaches the BU's database where the threshold notifications were created, rather than the register's local database (which defaults to LOCAL_ONLY).

Please let me know if you have any questions about these configuration steps!

Summary: Penny rounding not applied on Orders paid with Cash
Description: We enabled rounding for USD Cash to test the upcoming requirement to abolish pennies in the US and in our validation, we noticed Orders paid with Cash did not get rounded to nearest nickel.
Comments:
16/Feb/26 5:06 AM;712020:877ebe8a-e44a-419d-b0bd-b385e6a816f3;h2. Confirm configuration is correct (based on prior guidance)

From *US Penny Tender Removal and Rounding Rules*
[https://jumpmind.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/AD/pages/1590919170/US+Penny+Tender+Removal+and+Rounding+Rules|https://jumpmind.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/AD/pages/1590919170/US+Penny+Tender+Removal+and+Rounding+Rules|smart-link]

Previous fixes and configs expect:

* {{ctx_currency}} for USD to have:
** {{ROUNDING_STRATEGY}} = {{roundUpStrategy}} or {{halfUpRoundingStrategy}}
** {{ROUNDING_AMOUNT}} = {{0.050}}
* This is what actually drives nickel rounding; tender-level behaviour assumes the currency is set correctly.

*Suggestion 1*

Verify on the env where you captured the receipt that USD is configured per the example in that page:

{noformat}SELECT ALPHABETIC_CODE, ROUNDING_STRATEGY, ROUNDING_AMOUNT
FROM CTX_CURRENCY
WHERE ALPHABETIC_CODE = 'USD';{noformat}

If it’s still on {{defaultRoundingStrategy}} or {{ROUNDING_AMOUNT}} is {{NULL}}/{{0.01}}, cash orders won’t be rounded.

Based on prior penny‑rounding issues (JMCH‑1613, JMCH‑50 / JMCH‑3287, JMCH‑1473) and the _US Penny Tender Removal and Rounding Rules_ doc ([https://jumpmind.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/AD/pages/1590919170/US+Penny+Tender+Removal+and+Rounding+Rules),|https://jumpmind.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/AD/pages/1590919170/US+Penny+Tender+Removal+and+Rounding+Rules),|smart-link] this appears to be another flow where the cash‑rounding logic is not being invoked.

* USD currency is configured with 0.05 rounding (please confirm {{ROUNDING_STRATEGY}} and {{ROUNDING_AMOUNT}} in {{CTX_CURRENCY}} for USD in this env).
* Regular in‑store cash sales round correctly (please verify).
* For Orders (screenshot attached – item has Order ID and Ground Shipping line), the tendered cash amount equals the unrounded amount due and no separate “Cash Rounding Adjustment” tender line is generated.

Request:

* Ensure the same penny‑rounding logic used for standard cash sales is applied to cash payments on Orders, including generating a distinct rounding tender line with the correct tenderTypeCode so the receipt can display “Cash Rounding Adjustment”

*As per the previous tickets we found the solution and posted as internal comment is this the correct method can you suggest?*

Summary: When one of the items in a multi-qty line item gets a discount, the discount amount should be prorated when partially being returned.
Description:
see [https://jumpmind.atlassian.net/browse/JMCH-1615|https://jumpmind.atlassian.net/browse/JMCH-1615|smart-link]  for history



Currently if a customer purchases 2 items at $20 each and a promotion makes one item free, the total paid is $20. Internally, the transaction contains one paid unit ($20) and one free unit ($0), grouped under a single line item with quantity = 2.

When returning only 1 item from that line item, the system currently processes the $0 promotional unit first. As a result, the refund amount is $0. This aligns with the existing base logic to ensure the customer does not return the paid unit while keeping the free promotional unit.



However, we don’t want customer to be able to return 1 of 2 items and leave with $0 amount returned. The amount should be prorated to calculate the refund differently when returning one item from a promotional multi-quantity line item and expecting partial return($10 in this example)

Description:
In Canada, we need to present the card when voiding any card tenders. So, in Post void, we are prompted to present the card on the pinpad.
Here, if the user presses ‘X' on the pinpad, the auth void is cancelled, then we see ‘Unable to post void transaction' error on the POS. This is correct.

However, After you see ‘Unable to post void transaction’ and then you click 'Post void’ again, two things go wrong:
1. We directly see ‘Unable to post void transaction’ *without actually trying to void the card/transaction*.

# When we click on ‘Ok’ on the ‘Unable to post void transaction’ prompt, we go back to transaction details screen and the transaction shows up as successfully post voided.

Attached logs and screen recording.

For receipted return:

{noformat}Unexpected action "Scan".

24/Feb/26 12:32 PM;712020:0b3de8b9-fd84-40a7-a9ca-77e86f66a0b0;Here are some general guidelines for updating the logging output via Helm.  We don’t store the values provided during implementation, as customers may change these over time to fit their needs. 



  *Method* *1:* *Update* *Helm* *Values* *File* *(Recommended)*                                                                                                                                                                    

                                                                                                                                                                                                                     

  *Option* *A:* *Override* *in* *values.yaml*



  If you have access to the Helm chart's values.yaml:



  # values.yaml or values-override.yaml



  # Logging configuration

  logging:

    level:

      root: INFO

      org.jumpmind.pos.promotion: DEBUG

      org.jumpmind.pos.promotion.service.internal.InOperationEvaluator: DEBUG

      org.jumpmind.pos.promotion.service.internal.AttributesAnalyzer: DEBUG

      org.jumpmind.pos.promotion.service.internal.PromoHelper: DEBUG

      org.jumpmind.pos.promotion.service.PromotionCalculator: DEBUG



  # Alternative format (if using Spring Boot style)

  log:

    level:

      root: INFO

      org:

        jumpmind:

          pos:

            promotion: DEBUG



  # If UPE uses environment variables for logging

  env:

* name: LOGGING_LEVEL_ORG_JUMPMIND_POS_PROMOTION

      value: DEBUG

* name: LOGGING_LEVEL_ROOT

      value: INFO



  Then upgrade the Helm release:



  # Upgrade with override file

  helm upgrade upe jumpmind/universal-promotion-engine \

    --namespace production \

    --values values-override.yaml \

    --reuse-values



  # Or upgrade with inline values

  helm upgrade upe jumpmind/universal-promotion-engine \

    --namespace production \

    --set logging.level.org.jumpmind.pos.promotion=DEBUG \

    --reuse-values



  *Option* *B:* *Create* *ConfigMap* *for* *Logging* *Configuration*



  Create a ConfigMap with logback.xml or log4j2.xml:



  *configmap-logging.yaml:*

  apiVersion: v1

  kind: ConfigMap

  metadata:

    name: upe-logging-config

    namespace: production

  data:

    logback.xml: |

      <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>

      <configuration>

        <appender name="CONSOLE" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">

          <encoder>

            <pattern>%d{yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS} [%thread] %-5level %logger{36} - %msg%n</pattern>

          </encoder>

        </appender>

   

        <appender name="JSON" class="ch.qos.logback.core.ConsoleAppender">

          <encoder class="net.logstash.logback.encoder.LogstashEncoder">

            <includeContext>true</includeContext>

            <includeMdc>true</includeMdc>

          </encoder>

        </appender>

   

        <!-- Promotion engine debug logging -->

        <logger name="org.jumpmind.pos.promotion" level="DEBUG"/>

        <logger name="org.jumpmind.pos.promotion.service.internal.InOperationEvaluator" level="DEBUG"/>

        <logger name="org.jumpmind.pos.promotion.service.internal.AttributesAnalyzer" level="DEBUG"/>

        <logger name="org.jumpmind.pos.promotion.service.internal.PromoHelper" level="DEBUG"/>

        <logger name="org.jumpmind.pos.promotion.service.PromotionCalculator" level="DEBUG"/>

   

        <root level="INFO">

          <appender-ref ref="CONSOLE"/>

        </root>

      </configuration>



  Apply and mount in Helm values:



  # Apply ConfigMap

  kubectl apply -f configmap-logging.yaml



  # Update values.yaml to mount the ConfigMap



  *values-override.yaml:*

  # Mount logging config as volume

  volumes:

* name: logging-config

      configMap:

        name: upe-logging-config



  volumeMounts:

* name: logging-config

      mountPath: /app/config/logback.xml

      subPath: logback.xml

      readOnly: true



  # Ensure Java picks up the config

  env:

* name: LOGGING_CONFIG

      value: /app/config/logback.xml

    # Or for logback specifically

* name: LOGBACK_CONFIGURATION_FILE

      value: /app/config/logback.xml

  *Option* *A:* *Edit* *Deployment* *Environment* *Variables*

25/Feb/26 9:18 PM;712020:0b3de8b9-fd84-40a7-a9ca-77e86f66a0b0;The fix for JMC-8556 (the timezone-related initial load bug) is present and working correctly in your 243.8.8 version. The UTC vs. local time comparison issue has been resolved.

The initial data loads are starting (whereas before they would wait indefinitely because of the timezone challenge) — they appear to be taking 30+ minutes on average, with some running over 2 hours — and occasionally getting stuck at specific percentages. From your screenshots:

* Device 3040-012 has been stuck at 80% for over an hour
* Device 0174-011 is processing 2,950,082 records and has been running for 2.5 hours
* It appears triggers are being created quickly in these cases.  

This is a data volume and performance issue, not a timezone bug.

*A couple of questions before we dig further:*

# Is 2.9+ million records the expected data volume for your stores on initial load? That's quite a bit higher than typical — could historical data not be getting filtered, or is the full product catalog being synced?
# For the devices stuck at 80% — can you check {{sym_incoming_batch}} for any failed or errored batches? That stall pattern usually points to a batch processing error, a network timeout, or a DB constraint violation being retried.
# Can we confirm what version of commerce is running Centrally for these stores?  Are there accompanying Server logs for the issue?

*In the meantime*, for any stores stuck at 80%, clearing batches from {{sym_incoming_batch}} where {{status='ER'}} and restarting the SymmetricDS service should get things moving again.

To dig deeper on root cause, we'll need access to the SymmetricDS server logs at {{dtlr-symds.prod.jdna.io}}. Can you help get us access? We'll also want to run a quick query to see which tables and row counts are being included in the reload:

sql

{noformat}SELECT trigger_id, COUNT(*) FROM sym_data WHERE channel_id='reload' GROUP BY trigger_id{noformat}

After some thorough investigation, I finally understand where the disconnect here is on why your environment keeps showing this consistent issue. Your version of commerce is running Java 17. When we develop a fix for an issue, we develop it against our latest main/release branch and pick the fix down to the needed release branches. This main branch is updated to Java 21. Java updated their Common Locale Data Repository (Java CLDR) data between these 2 versions.

----

On Java 21, the currency for {{fr_CA}} locale is formatted to {{21,00 $}}

On Java 17, the currency for {{fr_CA}} locale is formatted to {{21,00 $ CA}}

----

We can fix the positioning of the currency symbol ($ CA) (so it is a suffix and not a prefix) such that it is consistent with the rest of the app - that’s certainly a bug. And will be addressed.

However, you may find there are spots within the app that do correctly show {{21,00 $}} instead of {{21,00 $ CA}}, and that is due the locale-aware money format being rendered client vs server side. 

* For example, the sales total panel will only ever expect money arguments for the totals shown and is designed in such a way that the money formatting/rendering happens on the client/in-the-browser.
* This generic dialog for “prompt over threshold” is supposed to handle any verbiage/markdown a customer may want to display and may not contain money information at all, so money rendering is done server-side for this specific scenario using the Java CLDR data for locale-aware formatting, which may produce some inconsistencies from the library doing the client-side money formatting.

If these desire is to only show {{$}} instead of {{$ CA}}, that would be an enhancement or could be customized from an extension layer.

Summary: JMC call to Adyen for "TransactionStatusRequest" not validating the current transaction ID
Description: POS will internally make a “TransactionStatusRequest” call to Adyen when it is unable to retrieve an authorization value for whatever reason. In some cases POS believes its most recent payment request was received by Adyen, but in reality was NOT (network failure, etc.), Adyen’s response will return an authorization message from the last successful authorization from the *last* transaction made by the same register/terminal, and POS will accept it and apply it to the current transaction without validating the transaction id from Adyen’s message. The transaction id communicated with Adyen consists of “YYYYMMDD<device_id><sequence_number>” (example 202602285119028729).
Comments:
02/Mar/26 3:48 PM;qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:41982bb8-9230-436f-9ab4-07119c50ecfa;[^2288-duplicate.csv]

03/Mar/26 11:20 AM;6299f8c41a2bdf007096c71d;This same issue has been identified and fixed in later JMC releases. I will backport it into this release. It would be available in 241.0.37.



For context, when we initiate a transaction/authorization with adyen, we generate a unique “ServiceId” to identify the transaction.

The root cause here is that in this very specific edge-case scenario when connectivity is lost between the POS and adyen, the POS thinks the trx is completed, but Adyen has no record of that.

After that, when we are making the transaction-status request to adyen, we do not properly set this transactions original serviceId in the correct spot. Due to that, adyen will report back the most recent transaction they know about

Setting this field to ask adyen for an explicit serviceID transaction-status will ensure only the active trx on the POS will have its status reported going forward

Summary: Request to add default query timeout in ConfigMap template
Description:
For the *Central* app, the {{queryTimeoutSec}} value under {{openpos.jdbc}} is currently hardcoded in the ConfigMap template. We'd like this exposed as a Helm value so we can manage it per environment without manual patching. 

Requested change in the chart template:

{noformat}{{- if .Values.central.enabled }}
apiVersion: v1
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: {{ include "central.fullname" . }}
  labels:
    {{- include "central.labels" . | nindent 4 }}
data:
  "application-helm-central.yml": |-
openpos:
  jdbc:
    queryTimeoutSec: {{ .Values.central.jdbc.queryTimeoutSec | default 120 }}{noformat}

With a default in values in yaml:

{noformat}central:

    queryTimeoutSec: 120{noformat}

This is actually already supported today, no chart change needed.

The Central chart (and all other commerce components) includes an {{additionalApplicationConfiguration}} value that lets you inject arbitrary Spring Boot YAML into the ConfigMap. It gets rendered as a separate {{application-helm.yml}} file and automatically activates the {{helm}} Spring profile, merging with the existing configuration.

To set {{queryTimeoutSec}}, you can add the following to your values override:

{noformat}central:
  additionalApplicationConfiguration:
    openpos:
      jdbc:
        queryTimeoutSec: 120{noformat}

You can use this same mechanism for any other application-level property you need to tune per environment.

Let us know if you have any questions or run into issues with this approach.

Summary: Ghost transactions still occurring in Prod for Adyen credit card authorizations
Description: Transactions are being authorized by Adyen, however Jumpmind has no record of payment request sent and transaction gets cancelled in Jumpmind.
Comments:
03/Mar/26 9:55 AM;632881baa84c7f79c3833b05;Claude analysis of the 0085-seq2051.JSON:

h2. What's happening in this transaction (Device 0085-021, Seq# 2051)

*The bug matches JMCH-1773 exactly.* The Jira issue describes: _"Transactions are being authorized by Adyen, however Jumpmind has no record of payment request sent and transaction gets cancelled in Jumpmind."_

The log file tells the story in chronological order (timestamps are nanoseconds, sorted oldest → newest):

# {{TransUpdatedEvent}} *—* {{ITEM_ADDED}} (~T+0s) An item was scanned/added to the transaction. Everything starts normally, transaction is {{IN_PROGRESS}}.

# {{TransUpdatedEvent}} *—* {{TRANS_MODIFIED}} (~T+0.5s) A modification was made to the transaction (likely a customer loyalty lookup or discount applied).

# {{CheckoutStartedEvent}} (~T+1.3s) The cashier proceeded to checkout. Transaction still {{IN_PROGRESS}}.

# {{BeginTenderingEvent}} (~T+54s, then duplicated at ~T+167s) The tendering/payment screen was reached — *3 separate* {{BeginTenderingEvent}} *firings across ~2.5 minutes*. This is suspicious and suggests the cashier may have attempted tendering *multiple times*, possibly due to a timeout or UI hang. Each attempt has no active span/trace ID, meaning *no payment request was actually dispatched to Adyen* from the POS side.

# {{TransCompleteEvent}} *—* {{CANCELLED}} (final) Despite the multiple tendering attempts, the transaction ends up {{CANCELLED}} in Jumpmind — never completing.

----

h2. Where the problem occurs

The failure happens *between* {{BeginTenderingEvent}} *and payment dispatch*. The logs show the POS fired the tendering event (and retried it multiple times), but there's *no corresponding outbound Adyen payment request logged* — no {{PaymentRequestEvent}}, no tender confirmation, nothing. Yet Adyen apparently processed a charge anyway.

This points to a *race condition or silent failure in the payment communication layer*: the Adyen authorization went through on Adyen's side, but the POS either crashed, timed out, or lost the response before it could record the payment — causing it to cancel the transaction locally while the card was already charged. This is the "ghost transaction" described in JMCH-1773.

The repeated {{BeginTenderingEvent}} entries (3 attempts, spanning ~2.5 minutes) also suggest the cashier or system was retrying, which could be *compounding the problem* by sending multiple auth requests to Adyen.

h2. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

Ghost transactions are caused by a null pointer exception (NPE) during successful Adyen
payment response processing. The payment is fully approved by Adyen, JMC receives the
approval, but crashes while parsing card details because Discover contactless chip cards
don't include an expiry date in the response. The existing GetCardData endpoint handles
this correctly with a null check — the authorize endpoint does not.

The result: the customer's card is charged, but JMC has no record of the authorization.
The transaction is shown as failed to the cashier, who cancels/suspends it.

h2. PROOF: ADYEN RESPONSE HAS NO EXPIRYDATE

From the raw JSON response in Pod Logs (line 767), the CardData.SensitiveCardData object:

{noformat}{"CardSeqNumb": "01"}{noformat}

No ExpiryDate field. The Adyen SDK's SensitiveCardData.getExpiryDate() returns null.

This happens specifically for Discover contactless chip (posEntryMode: "CLESS_CHIP",
cardScheme: "discover"). Contactless chip reads don't always transmit expiry date data.

----

* *Store-Level Sync via Symmetric Node:* Symmetric node should always sync at the store level. Although the {{prm_assigned_promotion}} table will contain {{business_unit_group_id}} at the CO level, the synchronization will always occur at the store level using {{tag_business_unit_id}}.
* *Group-Level and Store-Level Support:* We should support both *Group-level* and *Store-level* synchronization to ensure flexibility across different use cases.
* *Handling Cancellations via Wildcard Sync:* CO data will be inserted at the group level and then synced to BOs for all 6 tables at the {{tag_business_unit_id}} level with {{group_id}} as a wildcard ({{*}}). This approach is especially helpful during cancellations. For example, if *Group1* has 45 stores with an effective start date of *1st Jan 2026* and end date of *1st Jan 2027*, and a cancellation comes in for 5 stores, a new *Group2* will be created for those 5 stores with the same start date but an updated end date of *18th March 2026*. Since all primary keys remain the same and only the end date differs, the sync will correctly update the existing records at the BO level for those 5 stores.
* *Primary Key Design is Critical: for single table for simple promotion* When consolidating from six tables into one, the primary key design must be carefully thought through, as it will be the foundation for handling cancellations and ensuring accurate record updates effectively.

----

We should *connect over these points to discuss them* in detail. Please share your availability so we can align and move forward.

We wanted to explore whether it is possible to route data from CO to BO using the _group ID_ (covering multiple business unit IDs via the routing logic defined in {{ctx_business_unit_grp_lnk}} and {{ctx_business_unit_grp}}), while modifying the data during routing—specifically by setting {{business_unit_group_id}} to {{*}} at the BO level.

From a SymmetricDS perspective as well, since it creates batches for inserts during synchronization, there may be an opportunity to modify the insert statements by hardcoding or transforming certain column values as part of the routing/transform logic.

If this approach is feasible, it would help avoid the operational overhead of expiring existing group-based promotions.

With {{business_unit_group_id = *}} at the BO level, any future changes could be handled more efficiently. For example, if updates are required for a subset of stores (e.g., 5 stores), we could create a new group for just those stores and propagate the updated data with a revised end date. Since the BO-level data would remain consistent—such as {{promotion_id}}, start date, {{business_unit_group_id}}, and tags (which are part of the primary key)—only those specific stores would be updated, while the remaining stores would continue with the existing dates.

Please let us know if this approach is feasible or if there are any constraints we should be aware of.

Summary: Shrug error on store EJ (transaction search) for a short period of time
Description:
A handful of stores (20 as per tracking the specific error on the logs) experienced a shrug error when accessing Transaction Search on their POS.

The error pointed to the query “TransactionAllByDateRange”, and seems to calculate the “startbusinessdate” value using the “transactionHistoryRangeDays” value we setup in ctx_config, currently at 120 days. Effectively queries ranged from nov11th until today. Manually running the query shortly after the issue was actively being reported saw response times of almost 30 seconds. After a couple hours the affected stores reported not encountering the issue anymore. CPU and Memory metrics on DB server showed no abnormal usage, spikes, etc. 

first issue was actually reported around 8h20 in the morning so we can eliminate “concurrent” volume on the effective tables to explain this in my opinion.

Summary: Split tender with card & Mall cert mid void by selecting back option doesn't void the mall cert
Description:
A split‑tender transaction is performed using a credit or debit card along with a mall certificate. When the Back button is selected, the system attempts to void all applied tenders. While credit and debit tenders are successfully voided, the mall certificate tender is not.

Within the {{TenderOptionState -> onVoidAllTendersConfirm}} method, the logic first evaluates the {{requiredCreditCardSwipes}} collection. If entries exist, only those credit‑card‑related tenders are marked for voiding. As a result, other tender types such as cash or mall certificates are not voided in this path.

Only when the {{requiredCreditCardSwipes}} list is empty does the method proceed to the {{else}} block, where it correctly applies the void operation to all remaining tender types. Consequently, mall certificate tenders are not voided when credit card swipes are present, due to the conditional structure of this method.

17/Mar/26 4:13 PM;712020:03eb0e30-3eea-4831-9533-05d046229d05;Hi [~accountid:qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:dbfee442-d87a-4e86-9068-4321cb45b9e2] - Mitchell gave a response about this issue on [https://jumpmind.atlassian.net/browse/JMCH-1769|https://jumpmind.atlassian.net/browse/JMCH-1769|smart-link]. I’ll copy it below:

After some thorough investigation, I finally understand where the disconnect here is on why your environment keeps showing this consistent issue. Your version of commerce is running Java 17. When we develop a fix for an issue, we develop it against our latest main/release branch and pick the fix down to the needed release branches. This main branch is updated to Java 21. Java updated their Common Locale Data Repository (Java CLDR) data between these 2 versions.

----

On Java 21, the currency for {{fr_CA}} locale is formatted to {{21,00 $}}

On Java 17, the currency for {{fr_CA}} locale is formatted to {{21,00 $ CA}}

----

We can fix the positioning of the currency symbol ($ CA) (so it is a suffix and not a prefix) such that it is consistent with the rest of the app - that’s certainly a bug. And will be addressed.

However, you may find there are spots within the app that do correctly show {{21,00 $}} instead of {{21,00 $ CA}}, and that is due the locale-aware money format being rendered client vs server side.

* For example, the sales total panel will only ever expect money arguments for the totals shown and is designed in such a way that the money formatting/rendering happens on the client/in-the-browser.
* This generic dialog for “prompt over threshold” is supposed to handle any verbiage/markdown a customer may want to display and may not contain money information at all, so money rendering is done server-side for this specific scenario using the Java CLDR data for locale-aware formatting, which may produce some inconsistencies from the library doing the client-side money formatting.

If these desire is to only show {{$}} instead of {{$ CA}}, that would be an enhancement or could be customized from an extension layer.

17/Mar/26 4:24 PM;qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:dbfee442-d87a-4e86-9068-4321cb45b9e2;Thanks for the update, Allison.

Summary: PSQ-556 Promotions with groupings (Ex. buy 1 get 1 % off or buy 3 for fixed price) are not grouping the items to the customers advantage (when items are differing prices within the promo and/or # of items purchased leaves some not getting promo price)
Description:
POS: Promotions with groupings (Ex. buy 1 get 1 % off or buy 3 for fixed price) are not grouping the items to the customers advantage (when items are differing prices within the promo and/or # of items purchased leaves some not getting promo price)

*Promo 44436 (Buy 1 get 1 30% off)*

When items are differing prices within the promo - Ex.85638176 ($100), 30374459 ($68), 30234015 ($49), 30734515 ($28) (has issues if amount purchased > 2 even if there are 4, 6 etc.) 

+Ex. 1+

If all 4 items (85638176 ($100), 30374459 ($68), 30234015 ($49), 30734515 ($28)) were on the transaction we would expect items 85638176 & 30374459 to be one of the 2 groupings in the buy 1 get 1 30% off (and 30% off $68.00 (which is 20.40) then spread across the 2 items proportionally) and 30234015 & 307334515 to be the other grouping (with 30% off $28.00 (which is 8.40) spread across those 2 items proportionally).  Total discount to the customer would be $28.80 - but the customer only got $23.10 off b/c it discounted the 2 lowest price items (28.00 one (8.4) and the 49.00 one (14.70) = 23.10.

+Ex. 2+ 

 If 3 of the items were on the transaction 30374459 ($68), 30234015 ($49), 30734515 ($28) we would expect items  30374459 & 30234015 to be the grouping that gets the promo with 30% off 49.00 (14.70) spread proportionally across both items.  30734515 would be full price to the customer.  Discount total should be 14.70 but the customer is only getting 8.40 because the grouping seems to be 30374459 & 30734515.  

*Promo 44191 (Buy 3 for $24.95)*

When items are differing prices within the promo - 21714162 ($16.00), 30156307 ($12.95), 30227095 & 30227117 (10.95)  and amount purchases not equal to 3, 6, 9 etc. 

+Ex. 3+

If I buy all 4 I’d expect the grouping to be 21714162, 30156307 and 1 of either of the last 2 10.95 SKUs with the other being charged at full price.  So the customer pays 24.95 + 10.95 but instead it’s discounting 30156307, 30227095, 30227117 so customer is paying 24.95 + 16.00.

Summary: The commerce-pos deployment in our production AKS cluster (jmc-dtlr-prod) experienced an OOMKill event
Description:
h2. Overview

The {{commerce-pos}} deployment in our production AKS cluster ({{jmc-dtlr-prod}}) experienced an OOMKill event on *2026-02-24* after approximately 5 days of steady heap growth, ultimately reaching ~10.9 GiB RSS against a 12 GiB container limit (exit code 137).

The growth pattern (~1.2 GiB/day) is consistent with either a true memory leak or unbounded accumulation. Code and infrastructure review identified multiple contributing factors across application code, JVM configuration, and Kubernetes infrastructure.

*Current mitigation:* A daily rolling restart CronJob is in place (7:00 AM EST) to reset memory accumulation while permanent fixes are evaluated. This is a stopgap only.

----

h2. Environment

|| || ||
|*JMC Version*|243.8.8|
|*Java*|17|
|*Adyen SDK*|31.3.0|
|*Platform*|Azure AKS (ARM64 nodes)|
|*Container limit*|12 GiB|
|*JVM MaxRAMPercentage*|90% (Helm chart default → ~10.8 GiB heap, ~1.2 GiB non-heap headroom)|
|*OTEL Java agent*|Auto-instrumented via Helm chart|

----

h2. Section A — DTLR Proposed Changes Pending Jumpmind Sign-off

DTLR's ownership extends to container configuration files and Helm chart values. The following changes are within our scope and ready to implement — we are requesting Jumpmind sign-off before proceeding.

h3. A1. Reduce {{maxRamPercentage}} from 90% to 75% (Helm Override)

*Current state:* The Helm chart default ({{default.jvm.maxRamPercentage: 90}}) is not overridden for the {{pos}} service. With a 12 GiB container limit, 90% allocates ~10.8 GiB to the Java heap, leaving only ~1.2 GiB for all non-heap memory: metaspace, thread stacks, code cache, direct byte buffers, OTEL agent internal buffers, and native SSL allocations. This is the proximate cause of the OOMKill.

*Proposed change:* Add {{pos.jvm.maxRamPercentage: 75}} to our Helm values, reducing max heap to ~9 GiB and freeing ~2.7 GiB of headroom for non-heap.

*Sign-off question:* Is there any reason the {{pos}} service requires heap beyond ~9 GiB under normal load? Are there known framework behaviors that depend on the higher allocation?

h3. A2. Add JVM Flags to Container {{Dockerfile}}

*Current state:* The {{ENTRYPOINT}} passes zero JVM memory or diagnostic flags. Legacy on-prem configs included {{HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError}}, {{UseG1GC}}, and {{UseStringDeduplication}} — these were lost during containerization.

*Proposed flags:*

||Flag||Purpose||
|{{-XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=512m}}|Caps metaspace — currently unbounded|
|{{-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError}} + {{-XX:HeapDumpPath=/jumpmind/tmp}}|Captures heap dump before container kill|
|{{-XX:+ExitOnOutOfMemoryError}}|Ensures clean JVM exit on OOM for Kubernetes pod restart|
|{{-Xlog:gc*:file=/jumpmind/logs/gc.log:...}}|GC logging with rotation|
|{{-XX:+UseStringDeduplication}}|Recovers duplicate String heap usage (present in legacy on-prem config)|

*Sign-off question:* Do any of these flags conflict with the base container image ({{commerce-jre:17-bookworm}}), the OTEL Java agent, or expected JMC framework behavior?

h3. A3. Replace Memory-Based HPA with CPU-Based Scaling

*Current state:* The HPA scales on {{memory AverageValue: 8Gi}}. This is counterproductive for JVM workloads: heap committed to the JVM is rarely released, recently-restarted pods drag the average down, and OOMKill events can trigger a scale-_down_ rather than scale-up.

*Proposed change:* Switch to {{cpu: Utilization: 70%}}, reduce {{maxReplicas}} from 15 to 10, and add conservative scale-down behavior (1 pod per 5 minutes, 10-minute stabilization window).

*Sign-off question:* Does JMC Commerce have any guidance on HPA strategy for the {{pos}} service? Is there a minimum replica count that should never be crossed?

----

h2. Section B — Jumpmind Investigation Requests

The following items are in Jumpmind's domain (application code and framework internals). DTLR has identified these through code review and infrastructure analysis. Full details, code snippets, and line references are in the attached documents.

h3. B1. Identified Code-Level Issues in {{jdna-*}} Modules

||#||File||Line(s)||Issue||
|B1.1|{{RemoteProfileStatusMonitor.java}}|37|{{ConcurrentHashMap}} grows indefinitely — every unique {{profileId}} creates a permanent entry with no eviction, no TTL, no max size. A {{@Scheduled}} task iterates the full map every 10 seconds.|
|B1.2|{{AbstractAdyen30Endpoint.java}}|171, 310, 332|{{new Client(...)}} created on every payment transaction, allocating a full HTTP client, SSL context, and connection pool per call.|
|B1.3|{{AbstractAdyen30Endpoint.java}}|353, 354, 387|{{new ObjectMapper()}} instantiated 3× per response parse. {{ObjectMapper}} is thread-safe and intended as a singleton.|
|B1.4|{{JdaVoucherHelper.java}}|129, 135|{{JAXBContext.newInstance()}} called on every SOAP request. Generates accessor bytecode into metaspace — not easily GC'd.|
|B1.5|{{MailgunEmailReceiptEndpoint.java}}|262–263|Feign client (HTTP client + interceptor chain) created per email send.|
|B1.6|{{MaskingPatternLayout.java}}|74–77|Nested {{IntStream}} with boxing/unboxing overhead executed on every log event. High-frequency hot path.|
|B1.7|{{AbstractAdyen30Endpoint.java}}|381–385|{{String.concat()}} in loop producing O(n²) intermediate String allocations per payment response.|
|B1.8|{{AptosSearchCustomerEndpoint.java}}|34–35|Mutable instance fields ({{searchMethod}}, {{attemptedSearchMethods}}) on a singleton Spring bean — thread-safety violation.|
|B1.9|{{DefaultBarcodeManager.java}}|73, 97, 165–166|{{getDeclaredField()}} + {{setAccessible()}} called per barcode scan; {{DateTimeFormatter}} created per parse.|

h3. B2. Framework-Level Cache and State Accumulation (JMC 243.8.8)

The ~1.2 GiB/day growth rate is partially explained by the findings above, but a portion remains unaccounted for. We suspect the JMC Commerce framework may contribute through internal caches or accumulated state not visible in the application codebase.

*Request:* Please review JMC 243.8.8 internals for:

* Unbounded in-memory caches (device state, session state, config cache, event queues)
* WebSocket or HTTP session accumulation from active POS terminal connections
* Any known memory-related issues or fixes available in versions newer than 243.8.8

h3. B3. Spring Session / WebSocket Session Lifecycle

In a multi-terminal POS deployment, POS devices maintain persistent connections over the pod's lifetime. If sessions associated with disconnected terminals are not cleaned up, they accumulate indefinitely.

*Request:* Does the JMC Commerce framework manage Spring session lifecycle for POS terminal connections? Is there a known eviction or TTL mechanism active under the container Spring profile ({{base,foundation,integration,intellij,env,swagger-ui,container}})?

h3. B4. Helm Chart Default {{maxRamPercentage: 90}} for OTEL-Instrumented Containers

The Helm chart ships {{default.jvm.maxRamPercentage: 90}}. For production containers running the OTEL Java agent — which consumes additional metaspace, span/metric/log buffers, and gRPC connections — 90% leaves insufficient non-heap headroom.

*Request:* Is a lower default being considered for the chart? What is Jumpmind's recommended {{maxRamPercentage}} for production deployments with the OTEL agent enabled?

----

Summary: Promote - Requesting for an api to support search and override for our Customer Care system
Description:
Currently our customer care system has the ability to search for coupons and, if they are expired, override and apply the discount to the customer’s order.  

Please see attached screenshots.  There’s a screen where the agent enters the code in the *Promotion code* field and selects *Find Coupon*. Once found, a popup appears with the promo details.  Currently, to override, the agent enters the coupon’s expiry date in the *Promo code date override* field then selects *Apply*. This will apply the discount to the customer’s order but *_please note that it will not update the promo itself_*. Its only for this instance.

Also, if the coupon is valid, the agent can enter the code in the Promotion code field and select Apply, this will apply the coupon to the order.

Open question (and Ill get back as soon as i have the answer) When an expired coupon is overridden using a past date, are current promos applied to the order as well? with the overridden coupon discount stacked over them? or do we apply just the coupon discount alone?

Summary: Aurus: Gift card balances not always correct in db and on receipt
Description:
For gift card transactions, I think the remaining_balance_amount on the auth line item should reflect the amount left on the card after the current transaction completes. I think we should just be saving the BalanceAmount from the response to the remaining_balance_amount, rather than doing a calculation to come up with the remaining_balance_amount.

*Example 1:*

WHen doing a cashout, the balance is off.

First they did a balance inquiry on the gc, and it came back with 30.14:

POSID:00971001,APPID:TVSFixed,CCTID:lane3600,TransDetailsData:,TransDetailData:,CardNumber:600649XXXXXXXXX4374,CardType:GCC,SubCardType:GC,TransactionTypeCode:44,CardEntryMode:S,KI:NA,KIType:NA,TransactionAmount:0.00,RequestedTipAmount:,TipAmount:0.00,DonationAmount:,TransactionIdentifier:191241443888424535,ResponseCode:00000,TransactionResponseText:,ResponseText:APPROVAL,ApprovalCode:003014,*BalanceAmount:30.14*,AuthAVSResult:NA,…….

In the same transaction, they then used the gc to pay 25.92, Aurus returns the balance of 4.22, which is saved in the db correctly:

Summary: Remaining tender amount not updated for card tenders during refund
Description:
{noformat}In this return tenders screen, When paying with Card, the remaining amount besides Card in green does not change after making a partial card payment. This does work with Cash and Store Credit though.

Steps to reproduce:
1. Do a Sale transaction and tender with Cash($10) and Card($10).
2. Start a return transaction.
3. Do a partial cash tender of $2. In this case, the remaining cash amount in green correctly displays $10 - $2 = $8.
3. Do a partial card tender of $2. In this case, the remaining cash amount in green incorrectly displays $10. The paid $2 is not deducted from the total card amount.

Cause of defect in code:
In TenderReturnPoliciesEndpoint -> adjustThresholdsForAlreadyProcessedTenders() Line 233, there is an exclusion condition[isChargeCardType()] to skip over card tenders, which is causing this miscalculation. I'm sure this exclusion condition is necessary for some other case, but in this scenario, it is causing a defect.

In the attached screenshot, the card amount is green is supposed to be $5 - $2 = $3.{noformat}

10/Jun/24 2:56 AM;qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:17401b5a-6776-46e7-a537-faa542a2b6b6;Nathan, it is on the same lines.

25/Jun/24 4:36 PM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;[~accountid:qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:49a731c2-79d1-426d-8103-c9e1ec1ede1b], this is working as designed. 

The way percent off item discounts current work is that all reward items that qualify for the item discount are totaled and the discount is applied to that total.   The total is then prorated back across the reward items that qualify (and possibly the qualification items depending how the promotion is configured).   If there is a left over penny, then it is applied to item with the largest price modification which in this case is the first item in the transaction.   If we always applied it to the last item in the transaction then we could still be shifting the left over penny as items get added.

Here is two examples of one identical item being 1¢ more based on rounding.  Happens all the time in different retailers.

Summary: User Permissions: Refund - Cash refund for role less than manager level receiving msgs requiring manager override when the message/override is not required
Description:
RCL Ticket Reference -[https://logicinfo.atlassian.net/browse/RCL-913|https://logicinfo.atlassian.net/browse/RCL-913|smart-link] 

_RCL Description -_

Any user whose role has permission to do a refund can refund CASH (Manager, PT Associate, Stock/Visual).  

The Manager role can refund > = the amount originally tendered in Cash (> could apply in a split tender sale).  

PT Associate, Stock/Visual can refund up to the amount originally tendered on the sale txn with no manager role level intervention required BUT CURRENTLY a message indicating that manager intervention is required is appearing.  A  message I*S REQUIRED* if PT Associate or Stock/Visual role level associate attempts to refund an amount that is greater than what was originally tendered in CASH *OR* if they attempt to refund CASH (should it be an available tender choice) when cash was not originally tendered.


*-Ex. 1-*

*-Sale txn 1:  Customer purchased item(s) paying the transaction in full in CASH or US Cash-*

-Users with- +-manager (role) level permission-+ -can refund the full cash portion with the no issues / messages.-

-Users with a role of PT Associate or Stock/Visual (-+-less than manager (role) level permission)-+ -are allowed to refund the full cash portion-  +*-BUT CURRENTLY-*+ -are seeing a message requiring manager level intervention.  This message should not appear in this situation.-  

*-Ex. 2-*

*-Sale Txn 2:  Customer purchased item(s) paying a portion with for example Gift Card and the balance in CASH or US Cash.-*

-Users with- +-manager (role) level permission-+ -can refund the cash portion = tendered cash portion with the no issues / messages appearing. (Ex. Sale txn 2 is $20.00, $5 tendered in GC, $15 in Cash →   Managers can refund $15.00 in cash.)-

-Users with a role of PT Associate or Stock/Visual (-+-less than manager (role) level permission)-+ -are allowed to refund the cash portion = tendered cash portion-  +*-BUT CURRENTLY-*+ -are seeing a message requiring manager level intervention.  This message should not appear in this situation.  (Ex. Sale Txn 2 is $20.00, $5 tendered in GC, $15 in Cash → PT Associate or Stock/Visual can refund $15 in cash.)-

*Ex. 3*

*Sale Txn 3: Customer purchased item(s) paying a portion with for example Gift Card and the balance in CASH or US Cash.*

Users with +manager (role) level permission+ can refund the cash portion > tendered cash portion with the no issues / messages appearing.  (Ex. Sale is $15.00, $10 tendered in GC, $5 in Cash →  Managers can refund up to the $15.00 in cash.)

Users with a role of PT Associate or Stock/Visual (+less than manager (role) level permission)+ SHOULD NOT BE ALLOWED to refund the cash portion > tendered cash portion.  +This is a situation where they should see a message that manager (role) level permission is required+ - *BUT the message as currently presented is misleading*.  CASH was an original tender on the sale in this example and RCL does not have a threshold of $10.00 more than the portion paid by cash before the message should appear.  If we use the example of Sale Txn 3 (Sale is $15.00, $10 tendered in GC, $5 in Cash → As soon as the PT Associate or Stock/Visual user tries to refund more than $5.00 in Cash the message should appear referencing that they are attempting to refund an amount greater than the amount originally tendered in cash and need a manager to override.  

*Ex. 4*

*Sale Txn 4: Customer purchased item(s) paying in tender(s) that DO NOT INCLUDE Cash or US Cash.* 

If a situation exists where a user with +manager (role) level permission+ can refund cash (instead of the tender(s) used in the sale) no message is required. This level of user can do that refund in Cash. 

If a situation exists where a user with a role of PT Associate or Stock/Visual (+less than manager (role) level permission)+  attempts to refund cash (instead of the tender(s) used in the sale) this is a situation where they should see the message that manager level permission is required because cash was not an original tender and this is regardless of what cash amount they are trying to refund (no $10.00 threshold). 

_Last update from RCL -_

{color:#ff5630}*Issues in Ex. 1&2 are good now*{color}{color:#ff5630}.{color}{color:#ff5630} *Issues in Ex. 3&4 for below Mgr level are not resolved. They can refund more than the cash paid without having to get a mgr override.*{color}

_Logic Testing -_

The permission {{return.receipted.tender.past.threshold}} was added for each user but does not handle Ex 3 & Ex. 4. From testing in Commerce Base using user 2222 that does not have this permission, if a sale is tendered in cash, then a receipted return is performed for an amount greater than the base {{REQUIRE_PERMISSION_THRESHOLD}} of 10.00, a prompt is shown - “_The chosen tender CASH is not an original tender of the return items and therefore has a threshold of 10.00. Tendering more than this threshold amount requires additional privileges. Would you like to proceed with a Manager Override?”_

The current prompt is misleading as the original tender was cash. Wouldn’t the expected behavior be to enforce the REQUIRE_PERMISSION_THRESHOLD if attempting to refund a tender that was more than the configured amount and also wasn’t an original tender?

Tender return policy data attached.

Description:
RCL Ticket Reference - [https://logicinfo.atlassian.net/browse/RCL-1114|https://logicinfo.atlassian.net/browse/RCL-1114|smart-link] 

_Logic Testing -_

For the issue / refunding to a GC the {{AdyenActivateCardEndpoint}} / {{AbstractAdyenStoredValueEndpoint}} is not setting an auth code on the authorization in the {{parseSuccessAuthorization}}

Screenshots attached.
Comments: 01/Jul/24 8:12 AM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;[~accountid:60b9bbb248549e0069485164], Typically we return the Adyen {{PaymentResult.PaymentAcquirerData.ApprovalCode}} in this field. This does not exist on stored value requests. Is there something RCL would prefer be returned here instead?

01/Jul/24 11:27 AM;60b9bbb248549e0069485164;In the response from Adyen I do believe we see an approval code. In the screen shot it is the highlighted value in green. In this scenario, is that something that can be returned?

02/Jul/24 9:42 AM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;[~accountid:60b9bbb248549e0069485164] This is actually in the {{PaymentReceipt}} field, a receipt text block, in Adyen’s API. Specifically the {{PaymentReceipt.OutputContent.OutputText}}. 

This is not something JMC wants to include in our base code since it would require us to parse out that particular line of text from that field and we don’t want to get into that kind of practice since it is very likely specific to this payment provider.   We would recommend overriding the relevant Endpoints in RCL’s code that will extract out that “auth code” and map it to the Authorization.java object that those endpoints typically build and return.
17/Feb/25 9:59 AM;6049ca6fe19f91006957856d;Nathan, we checked, and we can’t override Adyen endpoints. I’ll pass on the message to RCL team.

Description: When editing promotion DORETCPN724V2-37, which has 350,000 codes, the system duplicated the promotion and created DORETCPN724V2-38.
Comments: 08/Jul/24 9:18 AM;qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:f4268760-4d62-41e4-91ba-3d3b9be4c7a9;!DORETCPN724V2-38 History.jpg|thumbnail!

08/Jul/24 10:23 AM;5f3a889073a268004d6bc030;This is just how Promote manages editing published promotions (which is something we generally advise against). It clones the promo, increments the number, and re-writes out the “new promo” and tries to archive the old one. Promote is periodically unable to do this cleanup step - unless this is causing them some sort of issue, the old promotion can just be archived safely.

08/Jul/24 11:22 AM;5f3a889073a268004d6bc030;Hey [~accountid:qm:d8936ec3-5736-46a1-a0a2-e185d8b412c9:f4268760-4d62-41e4-91ba-3d3b9be4c7a9], this is a consequence of how Promote manages edits to published promotions. It’s worth keeping in mind that a published promotion is actually written out and presumably in a position to be picked up by data synchronization processes and propagated out to other environments. 

Because of this, Promote actually duplicates the promotion configuration, assigns it an incremented ID, and then re-writes the promotion out to the relevant data tables. It will then try to clean up the “old” promotion by archiving it. Periodically, this can fail due to some uncommon scenarios and the old promotion is left unarchived. 

You should be able to safely archive the “old” promotion here without issue. As Promote was unable to complete the cleanup step however, it may be worth ensuring that your edit took place as you expected on the “new” promotion as well.

Summary: JMCH-268 - Child Tax Exemption has wrong tax amounts in tables and on receipt
Description:
When applying a “Child Tax Exemption” (or any other item group-based, as opposed to transaction-based, exemption), the selected eligible items are exempted appropriately, but:

* The {{tax_percentage}} and {{tax_amount}} fields for the exempted line’s {{sls_tax_retail_line_item}} row appear to be off.
* The {{tax_percentage}}, {{tax_amount}}, and {{money_tax_amount}} fields for the exempted tax group’s {{sls_tax_group_line_item}} row appear to be off.
* The receipt total is correct and reflects the amount charged the customer, but the tax group information reflects the incorrect, non-exempted totals stored in {{sls_tax_group_line_item}}.

For example, if two items are sold at $30.29 each and normally taxed at $3.94 each, and one of them is selected for inclusion in a Child Tax Exemption, the customer will be charged the expected exempted total of (30.29 * 2) + (3.94 * 1) = (60.58 + 3.94) = $64.52. Summary: Cancel Process button on fixed station breaks customer sign up flow
Description:
*Description of Issue:* When creating a customer profile and enrolling in loyalty on a fixed station, we are presented with the prompt to “Cancel Process” in the top right corner. When we select “Cancel Process”, we are given an option to confirm that we want to continue cancelling the loyalty sign up. The issue is when we select “No”, we did not want to cancel customer loyalty sign up process, the customer display clears the prompt of “Confirm your address” for the customer, so customer signup actually can't continue. Selecting “Yes”, is working as expected.

*Reproduction steps:*

# Begin a transaction
# Add a new customer
# Enter new customer info
# Select “Create”
# Notice that the customer display is now prompting the customer to confirm their address
# Select “Cancel Process” in the top right corner
# Select “No”
# {color:#ff5630}*ISSUE*{color}: customer display clears the prompt to confirm the address so we cannot continue with customer loyalty sign up. We are expecting the prompt to stay on the customer display if “No” is selected.

Summary: Configure Datadog to Helm Chart
Description:
Hi, 



Due to the ongoing performance issues we need the ability to dig deeper into what is slowing things down. Can you modify your help chart to integrate datadog to it ?

You can use the following as a reference and add it to your helm chart for POS, UPE and Central services. 


{code:yaml}apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  labels:
    tags.datadoghq.com/env: <env>
    tags.datadoghq.com/service: <service>
    tags.datadoghq.com/version: <version>
spec:
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        tags.datadoghq.com/env: <env>
        tags.datadoghq.com/service: <service>
        tags.datadoghq.com/version: <version>
        admission.datadoghq.com/enabled: "true"
      annotations:
        admission.datadoghq.com/java-lib.version: v1.37.1
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: <CONTAINER_NAME>
          image: <CONTAINER_IMAGE>/<TAG>
          env:
            - name: DD_LOGS_INJECTION
              value: "true"
{code}

23/Jul/24 1:53 PM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;An update has been made that will be part of release 242.0.15.
------
New Helm chart values exist that allow you to set labels for the resulting Deployment or StatefulSet and in addition a separate value was added to allow you to set values on the resulting Deployment or StatefulSet’s Pod Template. These labels are not included as the service select labels favoring the automatically generated labels for this task.

Labels can be set on a per-application basis, or overall using the default values grouping. Note: labels from the default section are merged with the application specific labels when rendered. You may use this to override the values of labels specified in the default section, however, you cannot override the internal auto-generated labels for the application.


{code:java}
default:
  additionalDeploymentLabels:
    k8s.example.com/environment: prod
  additionalPodLabels:
    k8s.example.com/environment: prod

pos:
  additionalDeploymentLabels:
    k8s.example.com/application: pos
  additionalPodLabels:
    k8s.example.com/application: pos
{code}

Summary: Promote - Enhancement to Coupon Code generation
Description:
NOTE: This may move up in priority as we will move away from the system we currently use for coupon code generation

We observed the following with the current code generation formula:

# The codes are predictable, ex. if we set the pattern as ####### then the codes are very simple and predictable - AAAAAA1, AAAAA2.  While these are single use codes, customers can figure out the pattern and use another code rendering it unusable for the intended customer.
# The codes repeat, ex. with a pattern of ####### the generated code of AAAAAAA is re-generated for multiple promos. A customer could mistakenly apply the code for an old promo but it could work for newer promo.

We could insert characters into the pattern but our users would then have to remember what patterns were already submitted, requiring them to jot the patterns somewhere.

Our requests are:

# To generate codes that are more random so the pattern isnt apparent to a customer, even when the pattern is all '#'
# Do not repeat codes, once a code is generated, the system should not generate the same code again.
