Summary: Tax | Taxes in certain states (AL, PA) calculate incorrectly for non-receipted returns
Description:
Alabama, and a few other states have percentage tax that applies unless the taxable amount is less than a dollar, in which case a specific amount is applied based on min/max range.

!image-20250512-135526.png|width=100%,alt="image-20250512-135526.png"!

This works correctly on the sale of items, but it is not adding this tax at all to non-receipted return items. 

To reproduce:

# Load the attached tax CSV files. I have updated store {{05243}} to use Alabama tax
# Update your item tax group ids to match what’s expected in the tax data
{noformat}update itm_item set tax_group_id = 'TPP/Goods';{noformat}
# Perform an even exchange transaction with a non-receipted item. Observe that the customer owes tax (the transaction balance should be $0).

!image-20250512-140445.png|width=1344,height=1301,alt="image-20250512-140445.png"!


----

The issue is here in {{CalculateTaxByFlatRateUsage}} / {{firstQualifiedRate}}():

!image-20250512-140622.png|width=100%,alt="image-20250512-140622.png"!

One of the filters is using taxableAmount, when it should be using absTaxableAmount.

Summary: Tender | Pre-swipe only works once per transaction
Description:
In TenderOptionsState, we set a flag to indicate that pre-swipe was attempted. 

{noformat}@InOut(scope = ScopeType.Conversation)
boolean preSwipeAttempted;{noformat}

The issue with this is that pre-swipe should be attempted again if you cancel out of tender options state and then press checkout again, but the flag has {{ScopeType.Conversation}}, meaning that it is stored for the life of the current transaction. (Would setting to ScopeType.Flow give us the desired behavior?)

To reproduce:

# Set openpos.tender.preSwipe.enabled = true
# Perform a sale transaction, press checkout.
# At the tender options screen, you should see the PED light up for a card swipe without needing to press the card tender button
# cancel out of tendering
# Press checkout again. At this point, the PED should prompt for card swipe again like it did the first time.

Our current integration plan is to leverage the order tables to push orders through the fulfillment process. Depending on the type of order and the timing of updates, we’ll make a call to the OMS to update the order accordingly.

To feed data into the JMC order tables, we're planning to create a new order controller exposed through the central service. The OMS team will send a request to this new endpoint when an order is ready for fulfillment.

# Performance Concerns – The OMS team raised concerns about JMC making several unnecessary calls, and this method helps mitigate that.

{noformat}INSERT INTO PRM_QUAL_ATTR_CONF (ATTRIBUTE_ID,DISPLAY_NAME,EDITABLE,ATTRIBUTE_LEVEL,ATTRIBUTE_TYPE_CODE)
VALUES ('grandfatherBenefitsEligible','ADP Grandfather program','0','TRANS','TEXT'){noformat}



For LIST attributes, each item you want to display as a list option needs to have a row in this table

{noformat}INSERT INTO prm_qual_attr_val_option_conf (attribute_id,attribute_value_option_id,attribute_value) VALUES
	 ('attributeId','uniqueId','optionValue');{noformat}

where{{attributeId}} is the value of the attribute_id from PRM_QUAL_ATTR_CONF
{{uniqueId}} is a unique identifier for the option

{noformat}<key>UISupportedInterfaceOrientations</key>

{noformat}<key>UISupportedInterfaceOrientations</key>

23/May/25 12:21 PM;70121:4c55edb8-b2f0-47f8-bb2c-524b3fa93eda;It looks like the reason these extended time periods are occurring is due to the Promotions cache being refreshed. This cache is being refreshed because the fixed register is receiving data from the business unit regarding a change to the prm_promo_code table. The first transaction rung following the cache refresh takes that increased time you have pointed out, however all following transactions occur much faster, with times as low as 781ms.

Did you modify the symmetric configuration to synchronize the prm_promo_code table down from the businessUnit? In the base JMC configuration, that table is only synchronized up from fixed to businessUnit to Corp. Is there a reason you have set this up to synchronize from businessUnit to fixed?

In addition to this, we noticed that in the application-override that was submitted, it looks like you have the following:

  promotions:
    cacheExpireMinutes: 0
    cacheRefreshCronExpression: "* 45 9 * * *"

The cacheRefreshCronExpression is formatted in a way we would not recommend. It should look something like "0 45 9 * * *". The cron expression you currently have will run every second at 9:45, where as the one that I typed does this once, at the beginning of 9:45.

Summary: Till Reconciliation | Do not close till until reconciliation is complete
Description:
There are a number of scenarios where reconciliation can be cancelled, leaving the till in a closed, but not reconciled state. BBW is requesting that the till not be closed when reconciliation is aborted via these scenarios:

{quote}# _Scenario 1: Click Yes on the Close Till -> Click No on the Reconcile Till - results in till getting closed but not being reconciled - this is considered as a 'Back' on the POS and would have to reconcile again._
# _Scenario 2: Click on Close Till -> Reconcile Till -> On the count till - press 'X' (Top right) - results in a second pop up, and close that as well, this closes the till but doesn't reconcile the register, resulting in having to reconcile again._

# _Scenario 3: Close Till -> Reconcile Till -> Count the amount and press Next -> Accept the discrepancies (if any) -> Press 'X' on the Pickup to External bank - this is considered a 'Back' on the POS, results in closing the till but not completion of the reconciliation process. This is what we've seen prominently in the logs._

_Out of the mentioned above scenarios - we've seen all of them when going through various incidents, most prominent are scenarios 3 and 2. And when they try to close the store they won't be able to do that since all the registers wouldn't have been reconciled properly._{quote}

When the till is in this state, there is no indication on the Open/Close screen that the till is closed, but not reconciled and the user will be prevented from closing the store until the till is reconciled. This is the main source issues for BBW, because they have the Mange Tills screen locked down to help desk users for use only when a register is down and a “force close” is necessary.

Summary: Weighted Item with Transaction Discount
Description:
* TPS recently started selling its first weighted item within Jumpmind. When the product is scanned, a pop up displays asking how much in ounces is being enters. The store enters the amount and the system adjusts the base price according to what is entered. This item is allowed to be discounted. The discount is being processed fine at POS, but when the transaction is sent into SA, the discount is being sent per ounce rather than total. For example, if the total discount on at item that was 4 ounces was $1.00 - the transaction in SA gets a discount line for a total of .25 cents, rather than the full $1. This is creating IF rejects within SA and manual clean up for our sale's audit team.


From Makira team:

We were able to reproduce in Test, but only when the discount is applied at transaction level. The reason is that the field where we look for the discount amount contains the total discount for the item when it is an item discount, but contains the per ounce discount amount (rounded) when the discount originated at the transaction level. This inconsistency in the JMC JSON data looks to be the problem.

We JM to look at this because how they determine the value that goes into the "modByAmount" field of the price_modifier is different depending win whether the discount is an item level or a transaction level discount. This only happens for the "sold by the ounce" items.

Attached File contains JSONs for five sale transactions. The weighted item in all the transactions has a regular price of $1.50 per oz.
seqNo 1829: 1 2oz item (3.00) with a 20% ITEM level discount. PriceModifier ModByAmount = 0.60 (the total amount for the item)
seqNo 1830: 1 2oz item (3.00) with a $1.00 ITEM discount. PriceModifier ModByAmount = 1.00 (the total amount for the item)
seqNo 1831: 1 10oz item (15.00) with a $5.00 TRANSACTiON discount. PriceModifier ModByAmount = 0.50 (expecting $5.00 but got the per ounce disc amt)
seqNo 1832: 1 7oz item (10.50) with a $5.00 TRANSACTiON discount. PriceModifier ModByAmount = 0.71 (expecting $5.00 but got ROUNDED per ounce disc amt)
seqNo 1833: 1 15oz item (22.50) and another "normal" item (14.40) with a $10.00 TRANSACTiON discount. Transaction discount prorated to 6.10 for first item and 3.90 for the second. This is correct. PriceModifier ModByAmount = 0.41 (expecting $6.10 but got ROUNDED per ounce disc amt)

Summary: Transaction publisher sequencing and timestamps don't always align depending on transaction type
Description:
Any "SALE" transactions in the QA Lab 0780 (DTLR) or 9740 (SP) appear in the sls_trans_publish table with a timezone_offset value of -07:00 while the "Management" transactions (Store/Device Open/Close) appear in UTC / Z.  Possibly this is a difference between what runs directly on the device vs a Central Service.  What looks odd to me is in the JSON for all those Mgmt Txns that we get from the Service Bus there's a discrepancy in the way the various Time fields are represented.  Specifically, the [createTime] appears in UTC, while the [lastUpdateTime] appears "localized".  And then the [beginTime] appears "localized" while [endTime] appears in UTC.  I do think that inconsistency is "tricking" out integration into sending timestamps to Aptos that are incorrect - leading to the problem they've reported that "Store Close" will appear to happen Before some of the Sales.

!image-20250530-215150.png|width=399,height=320,alt="image-20250530-215150.png"!

Here's a contrasting example with a Sale Txn where all the fields are consistently "localized" based on a 7 hour offset from UTC, and we can see the 7 hour value instead of 0 in the [localOffset] field.  I'm just not entirely sure why the logic is different based on type of transaction, and if we can trust the timestamps on those Mgmt Txns when they appear inconsistent:

!image-20250530-215216.png|width=361,height=388,alt="image-20250530-215216.png"!



Note: this is a 2-tier configuration where all fixed and mPos devices connect directly to the central cloud instance.



This could be also related to an issue observed with Order Create:

Reviewing the JSON out of JumpMind, there's an inconsistency with createTime and lastUpdateTime as seen here:

!image-20250530-220048.png|width=656,height=284,alt="image-20250530-220048.png"!

It's clearly showing UTC time for one and "local" time for the other, but there's no indicator of why one time differs.  If we look at the [transaction] section of the JSON, it also shows the "local" times and the 7 hour offset value from UTC.  Any idea why the only timestamp showing differently is the [order].[createTime] ? And should we just change the integration to use the [transaction].[createTime] instead?

!image-20250530-220102.png|width=665,height=440,alt="image-20250530-220102.png"!

Summary: Inventory: Outbound Transfer Document & Carton Numbers;  Formatting

We have access to what has been currently created in our APTOS environment as I want to call out we would want to avoid duplicates where we can.

Summary: Inventory: Unable to Edit Item Quantity or Remove an Item in Shipping
Description:
More of a functionality questions as we cannot seem to figure out how or where to do this - if a store is preparing an outbound document for another location - if they were to scan an incorrect product or an incorrect amount of said product, there doesn't appear to be a way to cancel a single item out of a carton unless you cancel the entire carton. We would need to be able to do the following with items being scanned into outbound cartons: (both of these do not seem to be possible and ca be recreated with the steps below): 

# Remove a single item if scanned incorrectly from a carton 
# Change the quantity of a single item without scanning one by one into the carton (i.e tapping and changing the amount). 

** Video attached

*Steps to recreate the issue*
Open Inventory 
Choose Shipping 
Select the plus in the bottom right and select transfer 
Enter a different store ID then hit create. 
Add a carton to the outbound transfer, and scan to add an item to the carton. 
Notice once the item is in the carton, there is no way to remove the item or change the quantity by hand w/o either deleting the entire carton or scanning more items in. Many times we want stores to scan, but they need the flexibility to change without scanning as well as removal.

Summary: Aurus - Pin Pad entry Method Options
Description:
Vitamin Shoppe has a need with Subscription transactions and Special Order transactions to capture a zero dollar auth/preauth for the purpose of getting a multi-use token for payment by our OMS.  Wallet (Apple Pay / Google Pay) transactions do not work in this case so we want to prevent tap as an entry method during the GetBinRequest with Aurus.  Aurus has provided the following guidance to support this.



In the GetCardBINRequest, the POS will send the *CardReaderMode* parameter to indicate which entry modes should be disabled. This ensures that when a customer attempts to tap their card on the payment terminal, the PED will not respond, effectively prompting the customer to insert or swipe their card instead.

Additionally, the POS can display a message in the Header Text, such as: “*Please Insert or Swipe your card*” to guide the customer accordingly.

 Below is the parameter Information:

 *CardReaderMode:* Attribute: 9N

 This field is used to handle the fallback scenarios in the screen mirroring feature. This field will be sent by POS to help PED decide which reader mode needs to be activated. This value will be as per below;

 

1 = Enabled

0 = Disabled

Bit 1 – Enable/Disable Tap entry mode

Bit 2 – Enable/Disable Insert entry mode

Bit 3 – Enable/Disable Swipe entry mode

Bit 4 – Enable/Disable Manual entry mode

Bit 5 – Enable/Disable Barcode entry mode

Bit 6 - Enable/Disable Camera entry mode

Bit 7 – Reserved for Future Use

Bit 8 – Reserved for Future Use

Bit 9 – Reserved for Future Use

Summary: JM Software not fully utilizing DB Resources on AWS
Description:
Today all JM Services including UPE and Store related services connect to the writer endpoint of AWS RDS Aurora DB even for read queries. This leads to a lot of unused infrastructure and puts additional load / stress on the single writer instance (Writer can only be one node at any given point).  This increases infrastructure cost as now we have to size the nodes such that each node can handle all traffic read/write instead of spreading the load out. 

In the past 6 months we have doubled database node sizes two times to account for this inefficiency. 
We would suggest JM to change the way their software works such that they leverage the  AWS Read Only Endpoints for queries that do not update database.  For e.g. in Java Spring framework you could create multiple dataSources and tie each one of them to a specific endpoint and use them accordingly. 

Attached is the screenshot which shows our DB resource usage in production at average load.
Comments:
13/Jun/25 5:31 AM;712020:e5b5ad7e-62d4-4865-986d-20a2966755ae;We might want to first analyze what are the traffic and where these database are coming from first, before rush into a solution like suggested  above. 

While this might appear to be an application-layer shortcoming, the root cause lies in the database architecture strategy. The current setup exposes only the writer endpoint to applications, without implementing a platform-level read/write separation strategy. This means applications have no choice but to direct all traffic to the writer, regardless of the query type.

In a cloud-native database environment, the infrastructure should abstract read/write routing away from the application, allowing services to connect through a single endpoint that intelligently routes traffic. Without such architectural design, even well-written applications are forced into inefficient patterns.


One possible solution in aws eks env for AWS Aurora is to introduce an Odyssey proxy: a lightweight, SQL-aware proxy traffic.

Summary: Transaction data is not saved correctly on an exchange transaction causing the published JSON to be incorrect
Description:
On an exchange transaction, if there are multiple sale items different than the exchanged item (not using the quantity key) the system is adding a quantity value in the sls_retail_line_item table in addition to each individual line.  This is causing the database to reflect more items were sold and causes the total numbers to reflect incorrectly and not match with the tender and change given causing the transaction to appear out of balance.

As an example:

An exchange of item 022538 (return/sell)
Purchase of 3 - 028882 and 2 - 031976
Total should have been 54.58 which was what POS prompted (and note the Tender of $60.00 and a change due of $5.42.
Yet the Total is 71.12 because the system added one extra 031976 item for $15.
The quantity key was not used and yet the sales retail line item table contains a quantity = 2 for one of the 031976 items.

!image-20250620-120210.png|width=380,height=643,alt="image-20250620-120210.png"!

28/Jun/25 5:45 PM;62d82941751c4f698e03958a;That is an issue. The sls_trans_publish and sls_trans_publish_status tables should be purged daily with no more than 2 weeks data. There is configuration in your purge process that needs added to clear those record out. You can manually delete data already published data, first the sls_trans_publish table and then the sls_trans_publish_status table. Deleting from sls_trans_publish_status when there is a sls_trans_publish record present will result in it being resent to Sales Audit.

28/Jun/25 6:29 PM;5c8fc1cd627d3b2d0163b7f1;Here are a couple sql’s you can use to manually clean up the two sls_trans_publish and sls_trans_publish_status tables, run them in this order.  Delete from the sls_trans_publish table first then delete from sls_trans_publish_status.

The first query deletes all transactions that have been published (a corresponding row in xx_status table) that were created over 2 weeks ago (14 days):

{noformat}delete from sls_trans_publish P
using sls_trans_publish_status S
where P.device_id = S.device_id
  and P.business_date = S.business_date
  and P.sequence_number = S.sequence_number
  and P.create_time < current_timestamp - interval '14 days'{noformat}



This query deletes all the status records that no longer have a corresponding publish record as they are no longer valid/needed there:

{noformat}DELETE FROM sls_trans_publish_status
WHERE NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1
    FROM sls_trans_publish
    WHERE sls_trans_publish_status.device_id = sls_trans_publish.device_id
      AND sls_trans_publish_status.business_date = sls_trans_publish.business_date
      AND sls_trans_publish_status.sequence_number = sls_trans_publish.sequence_number
);{noformat}



As always, you should test these in a lower environment to confirm.  You can update them to selects to verify the results before though be careful in prod with that much data the select may take longer than you want.

Summary: Inquiry: JMCPOS Treatment of Simple Promotions vs ORPOS
Description:
Background: We are using Oracle Retail Suite (RPM, RMS, RESA etc.).

In our migration from Oracle POS (ORPOS) to JMCPOS, we've observed differences in how simple promotions are handled.

* *In ORPOS:*
Simple promotions (Temporary Price Change) are treated differently from other discounts such as complex promotions, employee discounts, and coupons.
** Simple Promotion data (after completing a transaction) is stored in the {{TR_LTM_PRM}} table.
** Discount data (after completing a transaction) is stored at the line-item level in the {{COO_MDFR_RTL_PRC}} table.
** Notably, simple promotion discount amounts are not printed on the receipt. (Because it is a temporary price change and not a discount). 
* *In JMC:*
Currently In JMC, we handle simple promotions through dedicated promotion-related tables like {{PRM_PROMOTION}}, {{PRM_QUALIFICATION}}, etc.

----

*Our Request:*
We would like to understand how JMCPOS internally processes simple promotions, as Landmark has a large volume of them. This information is crucial to ensure consistent behavior and performance issues.

*Notably,* we send this Simple Promotion ID back to RESA in RTLOG (IDISC line) from the TR_LTM_PRM table in ORPOS and from the sls_retail_line_item_price_mod table in JMC), and it is essential to pass this entry to RESA.

09:06:07–09:09:36 (May 26, 2025) — Normal ops: till/session/status calls flowing on the Business Unit (BU) node.
(Observed in commerce-businessunit.log)

~09:10:57–09:11:38 — The BU’s OpenTelemetry agent can’t reach the in-store server (storeserver.instore.local:4317) several times (spans/logs/metrics export failures). This indicates a store-side network/path interruption around this moment.
(Observed in wrapper-businessunit.log)

09:11:36 — The POS client’s STOMP/WebSocket session to BU disconnects; BU marks device DISCONNECTED and publishes a DeviceDisconnectedEvent. This is the moment users perceive “white screen/freeze” at sign-in.
(Observed in commerce-businessunit.log)

09:42:20 — Device re-auths/re-personalizes and Session Connected appears, consistent with “reboot HTA fixed it.”
(Observed in commerce-businessunit.log)

09:43:06 — Client UI returns to Home; normal STOMP messages follow.
(Observed in commerce-client.log)

09:57:29–09:58:17 — Later, client shows loading/logout dialog and receives bursts of ConfigChanged/Status messages; UI stays responsive. (Not causal—just shows the session remained healthy after recovery.)
(Observed in commerce-client.log)

Root cause:
During username entry/sign-in, the POS client’s messaging session to the Business Unit server dropped because of a store-side network interruption (seen as repeated OTLP exporter connection failures to storeserver.instore.local:4317 just seconds before and after the drop). This network blip caused the BU to mark the device DISCONNECTED and emit a DeviceDisconnectedEvent, leaving the client UI in a waiting state that looks like a “white screen/freeze” until the HTA was rebooted and the session re-established; the subsequent re-personalization and Session Connected confirm that a restart restored connectivity rather than any code defect on login itself.

20/Aug/25 11:13 AM;712020:2d65c990-e57a-4a01-bb8f-03917cc4a81f;[~accountid:712020:a783ca19-9b70-462e-9e4e-f5b4741af810]    With the Store *2076* our observations based on Log files (May 25, 2025)

08:50:44–08:50:50 (May 25, 2025) — The client is on the sign-in flow: User ID prompt opens (seq 6416), then Password prompt (seq 6417).
(Observed in commerce-client-2025-05-25.0.log)

08:51:48 — BU is still serving device/till queries normally (IOpsService/Session calls).
(Observed in commerce-businessunit-2025-05-25.0.log)

08:51:50 — The client’s STOMP/WebSocket session to BU disconnects. BU marks device DISCONNECTED and emits DeviceDisconnectedEvent. This is when the user sees “white screen/freeze” on login.
(Observed in commerce-businessunit-2025-05-25.0.log)

~09:26 onward — Client is again receiving prompts/config updates later in the morning, consistent with reconnection/restart recovery
(Observed in commerce-client-2025-05-25.0.log)

Root cause:
During login at Store 2076, the POS client’s messaging session to the Business Unit dropped abruptly at 08:51:50; the BU immediately set the device status to DISCONNECTED and published a DeviceDisconnectedEvent, leaving the UI waiting for responses and appearing frozen until connectivity was restored. Logs show normal BU endpoint activity seconds before the drop and no server-side hang/exception at that moment, pointing to a transient client↔BU connection interruption (network blip or transport reset) rather than a login code defect.

*With the Store 2382 our observations based on Log files (May 26, 2025)*

Around 10:30 the register reportedly showed a white/login screen and seemed frozen. There are no server-side errors or disconnects recorded in that window for device 82382-000.
(Observed in commerce-businessunit.log)

Later, the client UI issued a Logout and cycled the screen (Loading → Standby) at 10:57:00, which fits the “reboot the HTA clears it” behavior stores are seeing.

The next login attempt at 11:46:13–11:46:20 was normal (username/password entered; authentication succeeded), confirming recovery after the UI reset.

Root Cause:
Client-side UI state corruption leading to a renderer/input freeze on the login screen, not a backend/session failure.
The strongest clues are the KeybindingService “undefined zone” warnings right before the forced Logout (these indicate the UI lost its registered input zone, so the screen looks present but doesn’t respond) and the fact that a simple UI reset immediately restored normal operation.
(Observed in commerce-client.log)

Summary: POS user access after promoted to the new role
Description:

usr_user table is updated with correct workgroup_id. However, new records being inserted with new workgroup_id in usr_user_workgroup table.
